08/20/2026 August 20, 2026 Australia 'outraged' over Israel declining to open criminal probe in World Central Kitchen deaths

Australia on Thursday summoned Israel's ambassador to protest a decision by its military to not launch criminal investigations into the death of an Australian aid worker during a 2024 Israeli air strike on Gaza.

Australian national Lalzawmi "Zomi" Frankcom was among a group of seven World Central Kitchen employees killed on April 1, 2024 when their aid convoy was hit in an Israeli strike.

The attack had drawn widespread international condemnation.

On Wednesday, the Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) said it had found no basis to probe the deaths of the charity's staff after a fact-finding and assessment procedure.

The IDF said in its report that it had mistakenly identified several individuals in the vehicles as Hamas militants and that the convoy deviated from its planned route. It concluded that "the decisions of the commanders did not raise reasonable suspicion of criminal misconduct."

Australia's Foreign Minister Penny Wong, who summoned Israeli ambassador Hillel Newman, said relations with Israel were "difficult" after the decision.

"This decision falls far short ​of the accountability we expect," Wong said, adding that Canberra was outraged.

Wong deemed Israel's move to not launch criminal proceedings into Frankcom and her colleagues' death as "especially insulting and hurtful" as it was announced on World Humanitarian Day.

"We do not have confidence" in Israel's investigation into the killings, she said. "The Australian government will continue to keep pressing Israel for justice."

Meanwhile, Newman after meeting Wong expressed "deep sorrow and grief" to Frankcom's family as he spoke to the media.

"Israel had no intention to attack or injure in any way the aid workers that were on the convoy," he stressed.

He said that Israel's decision was that there was no "criminal liability" and went on to say: "We must respect that conclusion."

World.title: Última hora de la entrada de inmigrantes a Ceuta, en directo | La policía desaloja la playa de El Trampolín y traslada a los migrantes a dos espacios habilitados
World.content:
“Extremar la higiene”: la Policía da instrucciones a sus agentes en Ceuta ante el riesgo de un brote de sarna

La Dirección General de la Policía remitió este miércoles a sus agentes destinados en Ceuta un díptico con instrucciones para prevenir y combatir la sarna después de que se haya detectado un brote de esta enfermedad de la piel causada por un ácaro. Según fuentes sindicales, al menos dos policías la han contraído. Además, el Ministerio de Defensa ha confirmado que se han diagnosticado 24 casos entre soldados del contingente desplegado en la ciudad autónoma, aunque ha recalcado que dos de ellos son anteriores a la entrada masiva de inmigrantes del pasado 30 de julio. Este jueves, durante el desalojo de la playa del Trampolín, los agentes llevaban guantes de un solo uso y mascarillas, como medidas preventivas.

El folleto entregado ahora a los policías recalca que la sarna “no es una enfermedad grave” y que sus principales síntomas son un “intenso y molesto picor” y la aparición de “surcos lineales entre los dedos, las muñecas, codos, axilas, cintura, muslos [y] órganos genitales externos”. También recuerda que las primeras lesiones dermatológicas “pueden tardar en aparecer un mes o mes y medio” desde la infección, que se produce por el “contacto directo”, que debe ser “estrecho y prolongado (piel con piel)”, con personas ya afectadas.

El documento, elaborado por el Servicio de Vigilancia de la Salud Laboral de la Policía, recalca que existen “tratamientos muy eficaces” que eliminan los sarpullidos a los dos o tres días de uso, pero que también es necesario tomar otras medidas cuando se diagnostica la enfermedad, como lavar la ropa que hubiera estado en contacto con la persona a 60 grados o, en su defecto, mantenerla cerrada durante cinco días en una bolsa, ya que los ácaros no sobreviven más de 72 horas.

Para evitar los contagios, la dirección general recomienda a los agentes que sigan los protocolos sanitarios. Entre ellos, utilizar guantes de un solo uso “en contacto con detenidos o presos y en el manejo de sus pertenencias”, “extremar la higiene de manos, uñas, brazos y antebrazos tras el contacto” y, “en caso de sospecha de contagio, acudir a su médico”.

World.title: Adiós lavanda, hola girasoles: un viaje por Burgos cuando en agosto cambia de color
World.content:
Cuando los tonos morados desaparecen de los campos, el amarillo toma el relevo en la comarca de La Bureba o la Ribera del Duero, con Briviesca, Poza de la Sal y Caleruega como paradas principales para descubrir el patrimonio burgalés

En agosto, Burgos cambia el perfume por la luz. Al recorrer los campos de la provincia por carreteras secundarias y caminos, el viajero aprecia una muda de color: la lavanda que en julio pinta hectáreas de morado deja paso a los girasoles, que colorean de amarillo vastas extensiones de La Bureba y algunos paisajes de la Ribera del Duero.

Quien quiera rodearse de miles de girasoles —esas flores que Van Gogh volvió universales— debe acudir durante esta época del año a La Bureba. Allí los girasoles aparecen a los lados de las carreteras, y se convierten en uno de los grandes protagonistas del paisaje durante unas semanas. Caminar junto a los campos en su momento más vigoroso puede justificar por sí solo la visita a esta comarca y sus pueblos.

Más información Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj

El mejor punto de partida para entender el paisaje estival de esta comarca burgalesa, que, además, fue de las primeras en adquirir personalidad dentro del condado castellano, es la localidad de Briviesca. En esta época del año los girasoles se muestran en su máximo esplendor y embellecen aún más al pueblo. Briviesca invita a detenerse y mirar los campos más allá de su condición de cultivo. La iniciativa Girasoles con Arte, puesta en marcha en 2024, combina el patrimonio urbano de Briviesca y el paisaje agrícola mediante dos trazados sencillos: uno de 1,63 kilómetros y otro de 2,67 kilómetros.

La plaza Mayor de Briviesca, en la provincia de Burgos. Teo Moreno Moreno (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Quienes deseen conocer más a fondo el ambiente local en torno a los girasoles pueden combinar paseos junto a ese paisaje efímero con una visita más detenida por el pueblo. La propuesta puede realizarse en medio día, y se puede iniciar con una etapa más urbana. Esta se desarrolla a lo largo de distintos puntos de interés de la localidad conocida como La Bien Trazada, por su plano ortogonal con forma de tablero de ajedrez. Comienza en la plaza Mayor, el punto desde el que la localidad muestra su trazado rectilíneo. En el centro se levanta un templete musical de estilo modernista construido en 1909. La siguiente parada está a escasos metros, en la excolegiata de Santa María la Mayor, iniciada en el siglo XIV y reformada en el siglo XVIII. La ruta continúa hacia el monasterio de Santa Clara, cuyo interior alberga un retablo de más de 20 metros de altura, tallado en madera de nogal y singular por carecer de policromía. La ausencia de color permite apreciar la minuciosidad de la talla, que bajo una capa de policromía podría haberse relegado a un segundo plano. Esa falta de acabado, atribuida a problemas económicos, terminó por convertirse en una de sus particularidades más reconocibles.

Retablo mayor en la nave central de la Iglesia de Santa Clara. Miguel Sotomayor (GETTY IMAGES)

Pero el encanto del girasol en La Bureba no se queda solo en Briviesca. El viaje continúa hacia Poza de la Sal, un recorrido que lleva al viajero a través de extensas hectáreas doradas cercanas a los pueblos de Quintanabureba y Llano de Bureba. En Poza de la Sal, el amarillo del verano encuentra un contrapunto mineral e histórico: una villa encaramada al borde de la llanura, con el castillo de los Rojas en lo alto y las antiguas salinas hundidas en el diapiro que dio nombre al pueblo. Conocida también como el Balcón de la Bureba, permite una vista amplia sobre la llanura de la comarca antes de volver a la carretera.

Un campo de girasoles cerca de Poza de la Sal. Architect´s Eye / Alamy / Cordon PRess

Al sur de la provincia, el amarillo cambia de compañía. Mientras que en La Bureba crece junto a cereales y llanuras, en la Ribera florece entre viñas y el recuerdo reciente de la lavanda. Después de la siega, la lavanda permanece en aceites esenciales, aguas florales, jabones, perfumes y otros productos elaborados en la zona. Así, Caleruega y Cilleruelo de Arriba han empezado a construir en el sur burgalés una pequeña cultura alrededor de esta planta.

Una calle en la localidad burgalesa de Poza de la Sal. Jose Luis Alvarez Esteban (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien se acerque a Caleruega para seguir el rastro dorado en los terrenos que circundan al pueblo entrará también en un lugar que no se entiende sin su más ilustre personaje: Santo Domingo de Guzmán, patrón provincial. Al llegar al casco urbano, el Torreón de los Guzmanes se yergue con 17 metros de altura desde época medieval sobre el resto de la arquitectura local. Le acompaña el Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, fundado en 1266 por mandato del rey Alfonso X el Sabio, que en su interior alberga un claustro gótico y el Pocito de Santo Domingo, donde la tradición sitúa el nacimiento del santo y al que se atribuyen propiedades milagrosas. En lo alto del casco urbano, la iglesia de San Sebastián, de piedra románica, vigila la plaza mayor del pueblo desde el siglo XII. De esta parroquia procede la pila donde fue bautizado Santo Domingo, trasladada fuera de Caleruega y utilizada en bautizos de miembros de la Casa Real española desde 1605.

El claustro del Real Monasterio de Santo Domingo de Guzmán, en la localidad de Caleruega. Blanca Saenz de Castillo (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Quien quiera detenerse más tiempo en la zona encontrará, además de los campos de girasoles que acompañan algunas carreteras de acceso, otros puntos de interés. El Sendero de las Loberas, de 10,2 kilómetros, permite acercarse a esas construcciones circulares de piedra que servían para resguardar el ganado de los lobos. En el entorno de Caleruega también aparecen otros vestigios, como los yacimientos arqueológicos de San Mamés y La Pudia o la Bodega de Alfonso VIII, vinculada al despoblado de San Martín de Bañuelos.

La ruta en busca de más hectáreas doradas por el sur de Burgos puede prolongarse por la Ribera hacia el pueblo vecino de Baños de Valdearados. Allí, la Villa Romana de Santa Cruz recuerda la huella de Roma en el territorio, mientras que a finales de agosto la fiesta en honor a Baco, dios romano del vino, llena el pueblo de togas, desfiles, mercado y vino de la Ribera (este año se celebra el 22 y 23 de agosto).

Celebración de la Fiesta a Baco, en Baños de Valdearados. Carlos Mora (Alamy / Cordon PRess)

Otra parada cercana es Villanueva de Gumiel, que permite prolongar esa continuación amarilla del verano por los campos de la Ribera. En sus calles se aprecian las fachadas de las casas antiguas, con una arquitectura caracterizada por plantas bajas de mampostería de piedra y plantas altas de entramado de madera y adobe. La iglesia de San Mamés, del siglo XVII, se diferencia de otras formas tradicionales al estructurarse en dos naves simétricas con ocho arcos cruzados y un valioso retablo del siglo XVI.

Recorrer con calma estos pueblos burgaleses permite disfrutar de un manto dorado que parece no agotarse desde la carretera. En estas tierras, la floración suele regalar sus mejores imágenes entre finales de julio y agosto. Y a quienes busquen mejores fotos suele convenirles acercarse al amanecer, momento en el que los rayos de sol iluminan de frente las cabezas maduras que miran hacia el este.

Como en toda floración agrícola, el estado de cada parcela cambia según la siembra, el calor y el momento de cosecha, por lo que conviene consultar con las oficinas de turismo antes de emprender la ruta. Y, sobre todo, conviene recordar algo crucial: estos campos no existen para la foto, son cultivos en activo. Hay que respetar todas las flores para que el siguiente visitante pueda admirar los campos de esta Castilla con la misma belleza.

World.title: Begur: el pueblo de Girona en el que se para el reloj
World.content:
Este enclave del Baix Empordà ha logrado conservar la magia de sus playas y calas, goza de algunas de las mejores propuestas culinarias del territorio y atrae por igual a locales y foráneos, permaneciendo en un ventajoso segundo plano a la hora de atraer al turismo masivo

Begur es una localidad catalana cuya fundación los historiadores acostumbran a situar en 1019, con la construcción del castillo de la localidad, aunque sus inicios datan de la época feudal. Ubicada a apenas 30 kilómetros de Girona, esta joya del Baix Empordà consigue permanecer alejada durante gran parte del año de las rutas turísticas masificadas que recorren parajes como Barcelona, la siempre bulliciosa Costa Brava o ciertas zonas del Empordà. Conserva además intacta su capacidad para sorprender al viajero y acumula un buen número de razones que obligan al habitual a seguir volviendo a su calma chicha. En verano la cosa cambia y la población, de apenas 4.000 habitantes, se multiplica por diez, pero, aun así, el pueblo se las ingenia para seguir siendo (relativamente) tranquilo.

Sa Punta, un establecimiento familiar totalmente remodelado de la mano de un grupo de empresarios encabezados por Daniela McLean —ideóloga del proyecto y con amplia experiencia en leyendas de la hostelería de lujo como el Palace Hôtel de Crillon, en París, o el grupo Peninsula Hotels—, se ha convertido en uno de los grandes imanes de esta localidad de cielos limpios y carácter familiar, con su apariencia de casa señorial en cuyo interior se esconde el espíritu de una beach house pensada para apagar el móvil, desenchufar el ordenador y vivir como si el mundo exterior hubiera decidido dejarnos en paz durante unos días.

Más información 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde

El jardín del hotel Sa Punta, en Begur.

Este hotel cuenta con 36 habitaciones, un spa, un restaurante con vocación transversal y sin delirios de grandeza (hay arroces, pero también hamburguesas), una piscina perfecta para los que desean ponerse en remojo en lugar de encaminarse hacia la playa y un entorno donde predomina el verde y una tranquilidad casi desconcertante, teniendo en cuenta los desquiciantes parámetros urbanitas. “Estamos en un lugar emblemático, rodeado de campos, de viñedos y de rutas ideales para darse una vuelta en bici o un buen paseo. Es un hotel muy tranquilo porque hacemos yoga y es solo para adultos. Siempre digo que es un hotel que transmite calma: pensado para desconectar totalmente del estrés. Por eso muchas veces insistimos en lo de la beach house para explicar por qué esto no es un hotel de lujo al uso ni un cuatro estrellas convencional”, explica Sandra Julià, la directora del establecimiento. “Tampoco estamos en primera línea de mar, aunque en cinco minutos puedas plantarte en la playa. Es una zona más elevada, así que tenemos unas vistas preciosas, pero con un ambiente mucho más íntimo”, añade sobre este establecimiento que abre de abril a octubre para adaptarse a las necesidades y deseos de su clientela.

La dificultad de acceder a Begur si uno no dispone de coche (el transporte público funciona en la temporada estival, pero sigue siendo complejo acceder al pueblo) se ha convertido, paradójicamente, en una de las ventajas de la localidad. “Totalmente. Lo cierto es que la gran mayoría de nuestros clientes necesitan coche para llegar hasta aquí y está claro que, si fuera accesible con el tren, el autobús y el transporte público, sería muy diferente. Y no solo para el hotel, para toda la zona. La movilidad aquí ya es complicada. Es cierto que a Begur y a Pals puedes llegar en autobús, pero no llega el tren. Eso hace que sea un destino un poco más exclusivo”, confirma Julià.

Vista del castillo de Begur. BORIS STROUJKO (Alamy / Cordon Press)

Más allá de las virtudes de un alojamiento pensado para el reposo y la desconexión, si uno decide salir de Sa Punta, Begur ofrece una triada insuperable: gastronomía, paseos y un sinfín de destellos del pasado. “Creo que eso es precisamente lo que la gente viene buscando. Pueblos medievales como Pals o Peratallada, lugares históricos, una gastronomía increíble, el arroz de Pals y unas playas preciosas. Todas esas pequeñas calas llenas de encanto”, aporta Julià. Pero a pesar del innegable atractivo de la geografía y la idiosincrasia que recorre cada rincón del Baix Empordà, Julià reconoce que algunos de sus clientes vienen buscando cosas distintas: “Por supuesto, hay de todo y también nos gusta que sea así, tener muchos perfiles distintos y ser capaces de atenderles con la misma solvencia. Hay clientes que vienen únicamente a jugar al golf. Comen aquí todos los días y no quieren hacer nada más. O los ciclistas, que pasan el día entero sobre la bicicleta. ¡Hay de todo!”, sonríe.

Para que no queden dudas, la directora de Sa Punta deja claro que en el hotel se prioriza un enfoque centrado en el adulto. El establecimiento es un gran reclamo para el turista familiar, pero solo con adolescentes, ya que la edad mínima son 12 años. “Por eso tenemos muchas parejas o grupos de amigos que vienen a darse un homenaje culinario, y no hay niños, pero pueden traerse a sus perros… siempre que no pesen más de nueve kilos”, aclara.

El bar exterior del hotel Sa Punta.

Para ponerse las botas

Lo del buen comer es casi una obligación para cualquiera que visite este enclave gerundense. La oferta es amplia, el producto impecable y hay un buen número de lugares que parecen sacados de una de esas películas románticas en las que los protagonistas se ponen las botas con el mar de fondo. AlKostat del Mar (en el hotel Finca Victoria) es uno de esos paraísos: con un coloso como el chef Jordi Vilà, responsable de los fogones de dos templos barceloneses como el Alkimia y Alkostat al mando del establecimiento, esta se ha convertido en una de las citas imprescindibles para los amantes de la buena mesa.

El chef Jordi Vilà está al frente de AlKostat del Mar, en el hotel Finca Victoria.

“AlKostat del Mar es un proyecto que puede adaptarse al territorio y es totalmente permeable a la cocina local. Casi podríamos decir que por sedimentación se acomoda allí donde llega. Creo que hacemos una cocina muy fresca, muy de olores, muy de sabores, sencilla: catalana y tradicional, pero siempre con nuestro toque. Como trabajamos mucho con el producto de temporada, pues hay mucho tomate y mucho pescado a la brasa”, explica Vilà. ¿Un plato imprescindible? “La ensaladilla rusa a la brasa, en la que cada ingrediente pasa por las brasas antes de volver al plato. Creo que explica muy bien lo que hacemos”.

Por supuesto, la competencia es feroz y en la lista de los favoritos de la localidad también sacan la cabeza tótems como Cap Sa Sal y la sidrería Mooma. Si hay ganas de aventura, Far Nomo, en Llafranc, es otra recomendación de primera clase y localidades como Peratallada, Pals y Calella de Palafrugell también ofrecen una gran variedad de mesas en las que ponerse las botas.

Para los amantes de los paseos o las calas, Begur es un seguro de vida: en el camino que lleva de Aiguablava a Platja Fonda puede recorrerse uno de los tramos más bellos del Camí de Ronda de la Costa Brava. El sendero transcurre entre pinos y acantilados, enlazando pequeñas calas y miradores naturales con vistas al Mediterráneo. El recorrido culmina en la mencionada Platja Fonda, una playa de arena oscura encajada entre altas paredes rocosas que sigue conservando una atmósfera casi mágica.

Si uno se queda con ganas de más, nada mejor que apostar por la ruta que lleva desde Cap de Begur a El Semàfor, un recorrido menos conocido que permite adentrarse en una de las zonas más agrestes del litoral de Begur. Un sendero que llega a una antigua estación electro-semafórica (la mencionada, El Semàfor), inaugurada en 1891 para orientar a los barcos de la Costa Brava. En el extremo del Cap de Begur, el edificio se abre hoy como mirador privilegiado sobre el mar.

Con tanto paseo, piscina, bici, golf y banquete, puede que en algún momento apetezca la irremediable tentación del dulce: para eso existe la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, uno de esos sitios a los que hay que ir dispuesto a dejarse aconsejar. “Abrí hace unos seis años y aposté desde el principio por la pastelería tradicional, pero reduciendo un 20% el azúcar. Abro todo el año y, aparte de brazos de gitano, coronas y pasteles como el de requesón (con queso local) o tiramisú con ratafía, mi producto estrella es el buñuelo del Empordà”, cuenta Anna Ferret, que regenta este palacete del dulce en la localidad gerundense.

Uno de los rulos de nata de la la Pastisseria Pa de pessic, en Begur.

La directora de Sa Punta quiere ofrecer a los interesados un último aliciente: “Tenemos un plus, que es algo que a mí me gusta mucho, y es que existe un gran sentimiento de comunidad que a su vez se traduce en una gran dosis de solidaridad: Sa punta forma parte de Costa Brava Centre y yo conozco a la mayoría de los directores de hoteles cercanos. Si tengo un banquete y me faltan sesenta platos, se los pido al hotel de al lado. Siempre nos ayudamos y eso me parece extraordinario en los tiempos que corren”. “Supongo que también es un buen modo de resumir lo que es Begur: un lugar en el que nunca te faltará de nada”, remata Julià.

World.title: Gangs suspected of stealing fire station equipment for ram-raids
World.content:
More than 60 fire stations have been targeted in the last year by criminal gangs who steal hydraulic equipment to use in ram raids.

One fire station in Sassenheim, near Leiden in Zuid-Holland, was attacked three nights in a row in the last week, while 10 sites have been broken into across the country in the last fortnight.

Police told NRC the thieves were looking for equipment such as cutting gear and hydraulic jacks used to free people who are trapped beneath rubble.

The machines can be repurposed to break heavily fortified windows used by shops such as jewellers and electrical retailers. Last week thieves left behind a hydraulic spreader that they used to try to smash the window of a jewellery store in Den Bosch.

The number of break-ins has jumped in the last year, with just 18 thefts from fire stations recorded in 2025 and 17 the year before.

“We are trying to strengthen our response teams and making detecting these crimes a national priority,” police spokesman Dick Goijert said.

Safety boards would not say exactly what was taken in the most recent raids because the police investigation is ongoing and to avoid giving “unnecessary information to people with bad intentions”.

Accessibility issues

Fire station managers have tried to improve security, but locking away life-saving equipment means it takes longer to retrieve it in an emergency, when a few lost seconds can make the difference between life and death.

Evert Jansen, a former burglar who now works for the police to raise companies’ awareness of the need to improve security, said he suspected organised criminals were behind the thefts.

“Unless they know how the equipment works it’s difficult for them to use it,” Jansen told NRC. “Maybe the burglars are stealing it on the orders of experienced criminals.”

World.title: Community remembers 17-year-old Lisa, but safety concerns remain
World.content:
Exactly a year ago, 17-year-old Lisa was stabbed to death while cycling home to Abcoude after a night out in Amsterdam, sending shockwaves through the country and spearheading campaigns to combat violence against women.

Lisa’s body was found beside a cycleway in Duivendrecht, between the city and her home town, where she was pulled from her bike and stabbed to death while she was on the phone to police.

Shortly afterwards, a 22-year-old Nigerian man known as Christ Jude was arrested at a nearby Amsterdam refugee centre. Earlier this year, he confessed to killing Lisa, along with the rape and attempted rape of two other women in Amsterdam.

A memorial organised by a village church and youth centre will take place in Abcoude Thursday, where people can leave notes or light a candle for Lisa.

Family thanks

That community support, said Lisa’s family in a recent letter thanking Abcoude’s residents, has given them the “the security and strength to resume our lives step by step”.

“Not by hiding us, but by continuing with everything that was so dear to Lisa. Let’s laugh, dance, toast and celebrate life as Lisa did—full of dedication, with a generous smile and surrounded by friends,” they said.

Lisa’s murder took place during the Abcoude Festive Week (Feestweek Abcoude), a five-day annual festival that this year will be held from August 25-29. Organisers have consulted with Lisa’s family, and a commemorative event is expected to be included in the programme. The family’s letter thanking fellow villagers will also be distributed in the program’s booklet.

“It is almost unbelievable that it will soon be a year since Lisa passed away. Our world collapsed and the impact on the town was also immense,” reads the letter. “Thanks to all the villagers for the impressive minutes of silence we were able to experience together. Thank you for the hedge of honour you formed during the funeral, we will never forget these moments.”

Moving forward

Since the murder rattled the country and led to national soul-searching on how to protect women from violence, some things have changed.

Municipalities have taken to designing safer public spaces with women in mind, with several adding more lighting and pruning back shrubbery for more visibility.

But for Danique de Jong, it’s not enough. She organized a “We Claim the Night” crowd-funding campaign shortly after the murder that raised more than half a million euro in three days, money that has been spent on policy, education and victim assistance.

“Many of these measures are about reducing the feeling of insecurity: mowing bushes and setting up a lamp. Then we feel safer, but it doesn’t make us safer,” de Jong told RTV Utrecht. “If we only focus on pepper spray, pruning bunches and hanging lighting, nothing will change.”

Mostly at home

While she said she’s hopeful and applauds the changes, she calls for a cultural shift regarding violence against women. “4.5 million girls in the Netherlands had to deal with sexual violence before the age of 18…[with] someone in their environment who does not accept ‘no’”.

That’s because violence against women mostly occurs closer to home. “A girl being murdered by an unknown person or man is very disturbing but doesn’t happen very often,” Roos Koolhof, a healthcare psychologist who works with victims and those at risk of sexual assault for Levvel/Qpido, told Dutch News at the time of Lisa’s murder.

“Mostly assaults happen in a familiar atmosphere—86% of the time—by the neighbour or your stepfather or a boyfriend or a friend or someone they meet on social media.

“What happens more often is a slap on the ass or touching someone somewhere they don’t like,” she says. “And that is what we should talk about so it won’t happen anymore.”

A survey by the youth news program NOS Stories found that many women feel unsafe in certain places and often carry keys to protect themselves against attack.

Christ Jude’s trial is expected to start in Amsterdam in January.

World.title: More permits issued for newbuilds but pipeline is filling up
World.content:
Turnover in the construction trade was up by 5.2% in the second quarter of 2026 while the number of newbuild permits was close to record levels, continuing the strong trend of the last 18 months.

Sales have grown by at least 5% in every three-month period but one since the end of 2024, although the market has cooled off from its peak of more than 7% aa year ago.

Newbuild permits issued in May, the latest month for which figures are available, stood at 10,824 for domestic houses and 2,637 commercial properties. The total figure is the highest since December 2024, when more than 13,600 permits were issued, statistics agency CBS said.

The number of buildings in the pipeline grew to nearly 234,000 houses and 48,000 commercial premises.

Permits are being issued faster than buildings are being completed, which has caused the pipeline figure to grow by around 33% for houses and 25% for business premises in the last two and a half years.

The CBS also recorded a steep growth in costs in the construction sector, with a 97% increase for domestic properties in the last year.

The agency said the spike was partly caused by congestion on the electricity network, which had prompted councils to speed up the planning process for newbuild projects before restrictions on new connections kicked in.

The labour market in the sector remains tight, with 28,600 unfilled vacancies recorded by the CBS. In the second quarter of the year 133 construction companies folded, five more than in the winter months.

World.title: Unemployment climbs to 4% in June, breaking downward trend
World.content:
Unemployment rose to 4% in July as the number of people out of work grew by an average of 2,000 a month in the second quarter, according to new CBS figures.

The Dutch government’s statistics agency recorded 404,000 people out of work in July, while the number claiming unemployment benefits increased by 3,000 to 200,000.

A further 3.2 million people between the ages of 15 and 75 – around a quarter of the potential workforce – were unemployed but not looking for work, mainly because they were retired or excluded by illness or disability.

Unemployment grew among men, particularly those under the age of 45, with 4% of men out of work compared to 3.8% in June. For women the proportion fell from 4% to 3.9% during the month.

The biggest increases were in eastern regions such as Twente, the Achterhoek and Gorinchem, while unemployment dropped in eight areas including southern Limburg, Flevoland and Zuid-Holland Centraal.

The total number reached 416,000 in February, its highest level for nearly three years, before dropping in the spring. A year ago 370,000 people were out of work while 164,000 were claiming unemployment benefit.

World.title: NEC hopes hang by a thread after Champions League home defeat
World.content:
NEC Nijmegen need a miracle to keep their Champions League hopes alive after going down 3-1 in the first leg of their play-off tie at home to Bodø/Glimt.

The Norwegian side showed all their experience as they withstood a second-half barrage by the hosts, while ruthlessly exploiting the handful of chances they created at the other end.

NEC struggled to break down their patient, well-organised opponents, but a late goal by Clement Bischoff gave them a faint hope of overturning the deficit in next week’s second leg in the Arctic Circle.

“They punished our mistakes ruthlessly,” team captain Tjaronn Chery told Ziggo Sport after the match. “It’s going to be a tough away game, but we’ll give it our all.”

NEC survived an early scare when the referee pointed to the penalty spot in the 11th minute after a handball by Bryann Pereira, but the video replay showed that Bodø/Glimt striker Jens Petter Hauge had touched the ball with his hand first.

The visitors went ahead in the 25th minute when Sondre Brunstad Fet finished off a move that began when Noé Lebreton gave the ball away in midfield.

Incisive

NEC pinned back their opponents in their own half while rarely threatening Nikita Haykin’s goal, while Bodø/Glimt looked more incisive on the few occasions when they broke through.

The second goal came from the penalty spot just before half-time after Tobias Stom pulled back Hauge’s shirt as the striker shaped to shoot.

Andreas Helmersen, who had drawn a fine save earlier from Gonzalo Crettaz, gave the goalkeeper no chance with the penalty.

Five minutes before half-time Haitam Aleesami headed in from a corner to leave NEC with a mountain to climb. But the home side refused to give up and got the goal their efforts deserved when Bisschoff touched in a cross by Dusan Tadic with five minutes left.

NEC almost bagged a second when substitute Kevin Kers saw his header come back off the post. But they will now have to succeed where the likes of Manchester City, Atlético Madrid and Inter Milan have failed in recent seasons by breaching the northern Norwegian club’s polar stronghold.

World.title: Online sleuth links Amsterdam’s “Lucky” to Canadian cold case
World.content:
An online researcher may have made a breakthrough in the hunt for the identity of “Lucky”, a man who collapsed in Amsterdam three years ago and is unable to communicate. A recent public appeal for information by the police has surfaced a potential match with a missing person in Canada.

An image of “Lucky”, who was also known by the name “Chris the Canadian” to Amsterdam locals, was likened to a file of pictures on the Vancouver Police Department’s cold case unit by someone on Facebook.

John Russell Kennedy, whose missing person’s file photos appear very similar to the one the Dutch police put out, was registered as missing since 1993.

Dutch police said they are considering the tip, according to paper AD, though they also noted that such similarities have been common in prior cases and turned out not to be real matches. “We don’t want to jump to any conclusions at this point, or to give false hope,” a spokesperson said.

Much of what is listed on the Canadian missing person’s case matches descriptions put out by locals who knew the man before his collapse in 2023. He was said to have a North American accent and appeared to have mental health problems.

Vancouver police confirmed they are taking the tip very seriously and said they had made contact with Amsterdam police, according to Anton van Straten, the person who made the connection online and shared it via Facebook.

“Only an official investigation, for example using DNA, can provide certainty about this,” Van Straten wrote in his post. “Now it is up to the professionals to investigate this further. In any case, it didn’t take me three years to find this potential match.”

If “Lucky” is indeed John Russell Kennedy, he would be 67 years old now and missing from his family for almost half his life.

World.title: Number of non-EU dentists in NL doubles in five years
World.content:
The number of dentists trained outside the EU who are moving to the Netherlands to help fill a chronic national shortage has more than doubled in five years, with recent arrivals coming from countries including Syria, South Africa, Turkey, Brazil and Iraq.

One in four dentists now working in the country qualified abroad, according to the dentists’ association KNMT, and in Zeeland more than half were trained overseas.

Figures from the Amsterdam dental school ACTA, which runs the admissions process for applicants from outside the EU, show 120 people are sitting its professional competence test this year, compared with 53 in 2021, the current affairs programme Nieuwsuur reported.

In total, 2,287 dentists with a foreign diploma are working in the Netherlands, a number rising by 150 to 200 a year.

Lack of national funding

The reliance on overseas recruits is partly due to a lack of education funding for Dutch students. Thousands apply but places are very limited. Etienne Verheijck, education director for the ACTA, called that “a policy choice by the education ministry.”

KNMT chair Hans de Vries called it “painful” that motivated young people are rejected by a lottery system, sometimes three times in a row, while the gap is filled from abroad.

The shortage is expected to grow, and the government’s own capacity advisory body has for years urged ministers to open more training places.

Checking your dentist is registered

To work in the Netherlands, dentists with a non-EU diploma must pass a competence test and learn Dutch before they can join the official BIG register of healthcare professionals. Those with an EU diploma need only meet the language requirement.

The healthcare inspectorate IGJ said it regularly receives reports of people performing treatments such as root canals without being registered. De Vries said dentists may work under a registered colleague’s supervision while they qualify, but treating patients unsupervised is improper and potentially unlawful.

Patients can check whether their own dentist appears on the BIG register, which is public and free to search. Dental care in the Netherlands works differently from many other countries, and full practices unable to take on new patients are already a common complaint.

World.title: Dutch boy, 12, seriously injured in fall in Austrian alps
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

A 12-year-old Dutch boy is being treated in intensive care after falling 30 metres (100ft) while walking in the Austrian alps.

Local media reported that the boy was walking with his father when he slipped and fell while crossing rocky terrain in the Tirol mountain range at 11am on Tuesday.

The pair were descending the Gänsekragen mountain after reaching the 2,914m (9,560ft) summit at 9.30am.

They were walking along a waymarked path towards a mountain hut in Winnebachsee when the accident happened about 500m below the summit as the boy rounded a corner.

The 46-year-old man managed to climb down the hillside to his son, who was lying unconscious, and raise the alarm. An air ambulance transported him to a clinic in Innsbruck, where he is being treated for serious injuries.

Police are investigating how the boy fell.

World.title: Poland tests 250 km/h train speeds for planned cuts to intercity journey times
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A speed of 253 km/h (157 mph) has been reached by a Pendolino train during tests carried out as part of preparations to speed up rail connections between Poland’s major cities from next year. The plans will see the journey time between Warsaw and Kraków cut to well under two hours. “Polish rail is accelerating – and 250 km/h is just the beginning,” declared the infrastructure minister Dariusz Klimczak, alluding to plans for Poland to later begin running trains at speeds of up to 320 km/h. Osiągnęliśmy 250 km/h na Centralnej Magistrali Kolejowej❗🚅 Dzisiejsze nocne testy systemu GSM-R na linii nr 4 zakończyły się pełnym sukcesem. Oznacza to, że pociągi pojadą tą trasą z rozkładową prędkością 250 km/h już w przyszłym roku❗ Pozwoli to znacznie skrócić czas… pic.twitter.com/ndXvePZP4t — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) August 18, 2026 The tests on the GSM-R data transmission system, a communication standard designed to be used at very high speeds, were carried out on Monday night. Trains will be able to run on Poland’s Central Main Line (CMK), which connects Warsaw with Kraków and Katowice, at a scheduled speed of 250 km/h from December 2027. That will cut the expected journey time between Warsaw and Kraków, the country’s two largest cities, by around half an hour to 1 hour and 52 minutes, reports rail news service Portal Kolejowy. It will also be possible to travel from the capital to Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, in around three hours. The fastest current connection is 3 hours and 30 minutes. Reaching the target speed of 250 km/h was a “very important moment for Polish rail”, said Maciej Kaczorek, a board member of PKP Polskie Linie Kolejowe, the state railway infrastructure manager, quoted by news website Money.pl. Poland has been operating Pendolinos, built by France’s Alstom, since 2014. The trains are designed to run at speeds of up to 250 km/h, but currently operate at a maximum of 200 km/h in Poland and run on routes connecting Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław and the Tricity area However, this week’s tests are not a record rail speed in Poland. In 2013, a Pendolino reached 293 km/h during a test on the CMK a year before the high-speed trains commenced passenger services in the country. A Polish Pendolino high-speed train has begun running in the Czech Republic for the first time. The Prague-Bohumín service will run until June as part of a certification process that Polish operator PKP Intercity hopes will lead to a Warsaw-Prague route https://t.co/hmUNd7ft0E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 10, 2026 Speaking to Rynek Kolejowy, deputy infrastructure minister Piotr Malepszak said that it had “taken too long” for the network to be adapted to allow regular speeds of 250 km/h. The current government, which took power in December 2023, has much broader plans for expanding high-speed rail travel in Poland, including building 2,700 km of tracks capable of carrying trains at 320 km/h. In December 2025, state rail operator PKP Intercity launched a tender for 20 such trains. They would cut the journey time between Warsaw and Gdańsk, on Poland’s Baltic coast, to around 100 minutes – from 2 hours 25 minutes currently – by 2040, Malepszak told the Polish Press Agency in June. Passenger numbers on Poland’s rail network have been booming in recent years. In the first half of 2026, a record 44.7 million passengers travelled with PKP Intercity, more than 10% up on the previous year’s record and some 45% higher than three years earlier. Poland has launched a tender to buy 20 trains that can reach speeds of 320 km/h (199 mph), making them the fastest ever to travel on Polish tracks. World.title: Polish government proposes middle-class tax cuts funded by increased rates for wealthiest
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s government has unveiled plans to reduce income tax rates for an estimated 3.5 million people earning around or slightly above average salaries. The costs of the cuts would be covered by increasing the tax rate for large companies and individuals with the highest earnings. The changes, which Prime Minister Donald Tusk says are intended to “provide relief and assistance to the growing middle class”, would come into effect from next year – when the government is facing re-election. However, the proposals still require approval from parliament, where Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, has a majority, and President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and has vetoed a record number of bills. 📊 Nowa skala PIT będzie lepiej dopasowana do rosnących wynagrodzeń. Do 130 tys. zł pozostaje stawka 12%, między 130 a 150 tys. zł pojawi się 24%, a 32% zacznie obowiązywać dopiero powyżej 150 tys. zł. 💰 #WięcejWPortfelu pic.twitter.com/1S2MpSkVoC — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) August 19, 2026 The main elements of the proposed changes, which were outlined by Tusk and finance minister Andrzej Domański on Wednesday, are an increase in the earnings threshold at which the lowest rate of income tax is paid and the introduction of a new rate between the lowest and highest earnings brackets. Currently, there are two income tax brackets: the first taxes earnings of up to 120,000 zloty (around €27,800) at a rate of 12%; the second taxes earnings above that level at a rate of 32%. There is also a tax-free allowance for earnings of up to 30,000 zloty. Meanwhile, anyone who earns more than 1 million zloty a year pays an additional “solidarity levy” (effectively a third tax bracket) of 4% on income above that amount. Under the new proposals, the threshold for the first 12% tax bracket would be raised to 130,000 zloty. For earnings between 130,000 and 150,000 zloty, a new tax bracket of 24% would be introduced. Then earnings above 150,000 would be taxed at 32%. Tusk noted that, since his government took office, wages in Poland have increased by around 30%, bringing increasing numbers of people into the higher tax bracket. According to figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, in June this year, average monthly earnings at companies employing more than nine people were 9,401.58 zloty, the equivalent of almost 113,000 zloty a year. “We’re not talking about millionaires here; we’re talking about a growing middle class…on whose shoulders the financing of state security, defence spending, etc. rests to a large extent,” said Domański. “We want to change this…so that those who work hard to earn their average wage can clearly feel the relief,” added Tusk. “And we want this to be financed by the wealthiest companies and the wealthiest individuals, who have the lowest tax burden.” The number of ultra-wealthy individuals in Poland has more than doubled since 2021, a faster rate of growth than anywhere else in the world, according to a new study https://t.co/MNKgmjzn2U — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 Therefore, in order to finance the middle-class tax cuts, Tusk and Domański announced that the government would seek to increase corporate income tax from 19% to 22% for firms and tax capital groups that generate annual revenues above €50 million. Meanwhile, the solidarity levy for individuals earning over 1 million zloty a year would be increased by one percentage point, to 5%. “I am absolutely convinced that this will make our tax system more equitable,” declared Tusk. However, he also conceded that raising the income-tax-free amount from 30,000 to 60,000 zloty – as his Civic Platform (KO) party promised to do within its first 100 days in office – would not be possible for budgetary reasons, in particular the need to finance high defence spending. Poland has introduced a new type of account that will allow individuals to invest up to 100,000 zloty (€23,200) tax free. The government says the scheme is designed to encourage Poles to build savings and channel money into the domestic financial market https://t.co/1xDHHJGYKX — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 14, 2026 The prime minister said that the planned tax changes would be discussed further this week at a cabinet meeting devoted to next year’s state budget, which is currently being prepared. The relevant legislation will subsequently be submitted to parliament, with the aim of bringing it into force in 2027. However, Tusk acknowledged that there is a strong possibility of a veto by Nawrocki, who has blocked dozens of government bills, including fiscal measures. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increase in the tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. Last month, he effectively blocked a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits by sending it to the constitutional court for review. However, he did approve a law increasing the corporate income tax rate for banks. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 Next year’s budget will be closely watched given that Poland’s fiscal situation has become increasingly problematic in recent years. In 2024, the European Union placed Poland under its excessive deficit procedure, requiring Warsaw to commit to measures to bring down the deficit. However, last year the deficit actually rose, from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to 7.3% in 2025, which was the second-highest level among all EU member states. This year, Poland’s public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time on record. The situation has led two of the big three rating agencies, Fitch and Moody’s, to shift Poland’s credit outlook to negative. This year, Fitch warned that the political gridlock between Nawrocki and the government was making tackling the deficit and debt more difficult. Given that Poland will hold parliamentary elections in autumn 2027, it is unlikely that either the government or Nawrocki – who will be supporting the right-wing opposition – will be keen on any fiscal measures that either raise taxes or reduce spending in areas such as social policy and defence. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. The country is already under the EU's excessive deficit procedure, requiring it to take steps to bring public finances under greater control https://t.co/LNJ0YrP2Ge — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland launches tourism campaign featuring Lewandowski, Eisenberg and Rubik
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has launched a new advertising campaign to promote itself internationally and attract more tourists from “key European markets” and the United States. The new initiative, which has the slogan “Poland. More than you expected”, features global Polish icons such as football star Robert Lewandowski, supermodel Anja Rubik, and Hollywood filmmaker Jesse Eisenberg, who received Polish citizenship last year. A series of videos, the first of which was released Tuesday, will aim to present Poland as “modern, safe, diverse and authentic”, as well as “defying stereotypes”, says sports and tourism minister Jakub Rutnicki. Commissioned by his ministry and launched by the Polish Tourism Organisation (POT), the campaign will be conducted in Germany, Spain, Italy, the United Kingdom and the United States. The first video promotes Warsaw, Poland’s capital, and features Lewandowski, Rubik and Eisenberg appearing near the city’s landmarks. Polish actor Nikodem Rozbicki, meanwhile, plays the role of renowned 19th-century Polish composer Fryderyk Chopin. In the 30-second spot, Chopin’s character declares that Warsaw is “where my heart is” – a reference to the fact that Chopin’s heart, preserved in cognac, was brought back to the city from Paris by his sister shortly after his death in 1849 and is now immured in a pillar in the city’s Holy Cross Church. Lewandowski, who recently joined US football team Chicago Fire, tells viewers that Poland offers “more than you expected”, a reference to the campaign’s main slogan, which suggests to viewers that Poland may surprise them positively. “Research shows that people who have visited Poland rate it much more favourably than their previous perceptions or media reports suggested,” notes POT in its press release. Magdalena Krucz, the head of POT, adds that she believes the campaign “will be as surprising to audiences as Poland itself is to tourists who come to us for the first time”. However, the slogan is not new: it has been used by POT to promote Poland since 2021. The new campaign will also feature Nobel Peace Prize winner and former president Lech Wałęsa, who led the Solidarity movement that brought down Poland’s former communist regime. POT notes that he remains “one of the most recognisable symbols in the world of the fight for freedom and democracy”. The music is arranged by Radzimir Dębski, better known as Jimek, a Polish composer and conductor who has regularly performed with US rap legend Snoop Dogg. Polish-American NBA star @JeremySochan has joined a campaign to promote Poland as a tourist destination. His appearance has been received positively, but Sochan responded directly to one commentator who said a black person shouldn't be advertising Poland https://t.co/KXDok7IAXP — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 15, 2024 Poland has experienced a tourism boom in recent years. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation, behind only Malta. The biggest tourist draw is the historic city of Kraków, which was last year named the best city break destination in Europe by members of British consumer association and magazine Which? for the fifth time. This year, Time Out magazine rated Kraków the 16th best city in the world. However, the country has a wide range of tourist-friendly destinations, including long, sandy beaches on the northern Baltic coast, mountains in the south, the lake district of Masuria, as well as many historic cities and modern museums and galleries. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 The city of Lublin in eastern Poland, which will be a European City of Culture in 2029, last year welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors, including over half a million from abroad. The city is known for its rich Jewish history, and featured prominently in the 2024 Oscar-nominated film A Real Pain, directed by and starring Eisenberg, whose ancestors were Jews from Lublin and the nearby town of Krasnystaw. Last year, the sport and tourism ministry announced that it wants tourism to contribute 9% of GDP within a decade, from about 5% now. The strategy includes creating a “Polish brand” through which internationally recognised athletes, artists, historical figures and products are showcased more prominently. Last month, the government appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. The city of Lublin in eastern Poland welcomed a record 2.2 million visitors in 2025. That included 506,000 from abroad, which was also the highest ever figure, with Brits, Israelis and Americans the most common foreign visitors https://t.co/6yMrRcf6ml — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 28, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Warsaw Uprising veteran and activist Wanda Traczyk-Stawska dies aged 99
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Wanda Traczyk-Stawska, a veteran of the Warsaw Uprising against Nazi-German occupation during World War Two, has died aged 99. Traczyk-Stawska, who survived imprisonment in German camps after the uprising, in her later years became a vocal advocate for the rights of women and disabled people. “Warsaw has lost someone extraordinary,” wrote Warsaw’s mayor, Rafał Trzaskowski, announcing her death on Wednesday. “A heroine, a soldier…but above all a teacher who, throughout her life, taught us what matters most: courage, dignity, and responsibility for our fellow human beings.” Odeszła Pani Wanda. Trudno w to uwierzyć. Warszawa straciła kogoś wyjątkowego – Bohaterkę, żołnierkę Powstania Warszawskiego, Honorową Obywatelkę miasta. Ale przede wszystkim nauczycielkę, która przez całe życie uczyła nas tego, co najważniejsze: odwagi, godności i… pic.twitter.com/uSNcsZ7c1P — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) August 19, 2026 Traczyk-Stawska, born in Warsaw in 1927, was only 12 years old when Nazi Germany invaded Poland. She initially became involved in the Grey Ranks (Szare Szeregi), an underground resistance movement associated with the Polish scouting movement, participating in sabotage operations. She later joined the Home Army (AK), Poland’s main resistance force, and, at the age of 17, served as a riflewoman and liaison during the Warsaw Uprising, taking the nom de guerre “Pączek” (meaning “Bud”). Traczyk-Stawska was seriously injured while fighting in the uprising. After the revolt was defeated, she was taken prisoner and subsequently held in various prisoner-of-war camps in Germany until the end of the war. After returning to Poland, Traczyk-Stawska earned a degree in psychology and began working as a teacher of disabled children in Warsaw. At the same time, she became an active figure in commemorating the uprising and its participants. In her final years, Traczyk-Stawska also became politically active. In 2018, she visited parliament to support a protest by disabled people and their carers, who were seeking more state support. Two years later, at the age of 93, she and another female uprising veteran, Hanna Stadnik, joined the mass Women’s Strike protests that broke out in response to the introduction of a near-total ban on abortion under the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. “We women will not relent this time,” she told broadcaster TVN at the time. “In the uprising, we fought for our freedom, because there is no dignity without freedom. If we are currently treated like incubators, we have the right to fight for our dignity…We will fight – unarmed, but to the last woman – not to be treated like objects.” Traczyk-Stawska was also among a group of female Uprising veterans who that year criticised PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński for wearing, during a speech condemning the Women’s Strike protests, a badge featuring the anchor symbol that was used by the Home Army during the war. She was also an advocate for women’s rights more broadly. In 2023, in a speech at the 79th anniversary of the uprising, Traczyk-Stawska noted that, “at the beginning, the generals shouted: ‘Why do we need so many women?'” But, by the time the uprising ended, “we had been given the same rights as boys. And we won’t get rid of these rights. Because everyone, whether a man or a woman, is a citizen of this country and has equality written into the constitution”. Her speech then became overtly political, saying that “this [PiS] government needs to be completely changed, as it doesn’t remember that women have their own position enshrined in the constitution. That we are equal to men.” In both the 2020 and 2025 presidential elections, Traczyk-Stawska expressed support for the candidacy of Trzaskowski, who is a deputy leader of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that is PiS’s main opponent. However, in both elections, Trzaskowski lost to PiS-backed candidates. Odeszła Wanda Traczyk-Stawska ps. „Pączek” – Bohaterka, Patriotka, wzór odwagi i niezłomności. Pokazywała, że prawdziwy patriotyzm to budowanie wspólnoty, empatia i otwartość na świat. Cześć Jej pamięci! 🕯️🤍 Najgłębsze wyrazy współczucia dla Bliskich. pic.twitter.com/nY0ijDSBlJ — Monika Sikora ⚡️ (@Moni_Sikora) August 19, 2026 Following news of Traczyk-Stawska’s death, many prominent figures paid tribute to her, in particular from the current KO-led ruling coalition. “Farewell, heroine,” wrote KO leader and Prime Minister Donald Tusk, sharing a photo of himself with Traczyk-Stawska and quoting one of her statements: “Do not stand, do not watch when evil happens, but react immediately, for that is your duty.” While she had fought against German occupation, Traczyk-Stawska later called for reconciliation. In her 2023 speech, she called Germany “our best neighbour” and said that the two countries must now “stand together”, including supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression. Today, Germany’s ambassador to Poland, Miguel Berger, expressed his “great sadness” at Traczyk-Stawska’s death, calling her an “advocate of dialogue in the process of Polish-German reconciliation and a passionate champion of peace, freedom, and human dignity”. „Nie stój, nie patrz, gdy się zło dzieje, tylko reaguj natychmiast, bo to jest twój obowiązek." – Wanda Traczyk-Stawska Żegnaj, Bohaterko. pic.twitter.com/MhfqlszVcI — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) August 19, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland “99% sure” fugitive opposition politician is in pro-Russian breakaway region of Moldova
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s prime minister, Donald Tusk, says that they are “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia. Last week, judicial authorities in Poland confirmed that they had received a letter purportedly from Romanowski, who is wanted in Poland for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served as a deputy justice minister in the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. In the document, Romanowski claimed to be in Transnistria and requested safe passage back to Poland. However, as the authenticity of the letter had not been confirmed, some media outlets speculated that the politician may not, in fact, be in Transnistria. Meanwhile, the Moldovan authorities quickly announced that they had no record of Romanowski travelling to Transnistria, which is a landlocked territory that only has borders with Moldova and Ukraine and operates no commercial passenger flights. A former government minister who fled criminal charges in Poland appears to be in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links with Russia. Marcin Romanowski's whereabouts have been unknown since he left Hungary earlier this year https://t.co/MPWroFVbMe — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 13, 2026 Speaking on Tuesday morning, Przemysław Nowak, spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, said they have “still not confirmed” the veracity of Romanowski’s claim to be in Transnistria, reported broadcaster RMF. However, shortly afterwards, speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said he wanted to address the issue given there has been “a great deal of speculation and misinformation regarding Mr Romanowski and his whereabouts”. “I can say that the intelligence services of other countries in the region with which we cooperate have confirmed to us the information that Mr Romanowski is 99% certain – I say that just in case – to be in Transnistria, in Tiraspol,” he continued, referring to the capital of the breakaway region. "Pan Romanowski znajduje się na 99 procent w Naddniestrzu. Chyba nie trzeba tu komentarzy" Donald Tusk podczas posiedzenia rządu ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/muVQVKrOTs — tvp.info 🇵🇱 (@tvp_info) August 18, 2026 Transnistria is a narrow strip of land in eastern Moldova that sought to become a separate state in the early 1990s as the Soviet Union collapsed, fighting a war between 1990 and 1992. Today, the territory, which has a population of around 360,000, operates as a de facto state but is not recognised by any other country. Its flag and national emblem feature the Soviet hammer and sickle. Transnistria has close ties with Russia, which maintains a military “peacekeeping” force there. Various experts and former intelligence officials have noted that it would be impossible for Romanowski to enter without Russia’s approval. The fact that Romanowski appears to be hiding there has led to criticism of PiS, the party Romanowski still technically serves as an MP and which publicly takes a strongly anti-Russian position. “If it is true that [Romanowski] is in Transnistria, a republic not recognised by anyone, de facto controlled 100% by Russia, then it must have happened through and with the participation of Russia,” said defence minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz last week. “Escaping under the Russian umbrella is the worst possible thing, because not only are they cowardly, but they are also joining the enemy of Poland,” he added. In his remarks today, Tusk said that Romanowski’s likely presence in Transnistria “speaks for itself regarding not only Mr Romanowski but the entire political group that covered up for and benefited from such people, and continues to cover up for them”. PiS politicians have largely avoided commenting, noting that it has not been confirmed that Romanowski is in Transnistria. However, deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek last week admitted that, if Romanowski did trael there, he would have “crossed a line”. Nie wyprzedzajmy faktów – powiedział poseł PiS Zbigniew Kuźmiuk, pytany, czy Marcin Romanowski może zostać zawieszony w partii.https://t.co/IQzuS8Ad7O — tvn24 (@tvn24) August 14, 2026 Romanowski served as a deputy justice minister in the former PiS government from 2019 until 2023, when the party lost power to a new ruling coalition led by Tusk. In 2024, prosecutors announced that they wanted to charge him with 11 crimes, including participating in an organised criminal group and using crime as a source of income. However, he instead fled to Hungary, where he was granted asylum by the then-government of Viktor Orbán, a PiS ally. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, his successor, Péter Magyar, promised to extradite both Romanowski and Zbigniew Ziobro, the former PiS justice minister who had also fled criminal charges in Poland and been granted asylum by Orbán. However, as Magyar was sworn in as the new prime minister, Ziobro fled to the United States, where he remains, and Romanowski disappeared, leading to months of speculation as to his whereabouts. Both politicians deny the accusations against them and claim to be victims of political persecution by Tusk’s government. Poland has formally asked the US to detain and extradite former justice minister @ZiobroPL, who faces multiple criminal charges. He denies wrongdoing and calls the case political revengehttps://t.co/BXdQgWm61q — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In his comments on Tuesday morning, Nowak said that prosecutors had found “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. Polish prosecutors are still, however, attempting to confirm Romanowski’s whereabouts and secure his extradition to Poland to face justice. He is subject to a European Arrest Warrant. However, that applies only in EU countries, and Moldova is not a member of the bloc. World.title: FedEx-led €7.8bn takeover of Polish delivery giant InPost wins EU approval
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Commission has granted approval for a consortium led by American transportation conglomerate FedEx to take over Polish delivery giant InPost in a deal worth €7.8 billion (33.7 billion zloty). InPost, which operates in France, Spain, the UK, Portugal, Italy and the Benelux countries, as well as in its home market, confirmed on Tuesday that it had received the green light from the EU for the deal, which was announced in February. If it goes through, the takeover will see a consortium made up of FedEx along with existing InPost investors, Advent, A&R, and PPF, purchase all of the company’s shares at a price of €15.60 each. Konsorcjum inwestorów, w którym jednym z uczestników jest amerykański @FedEx, uzyskało bezwarunkową zgodę KE na nabycie wszystkich akcji @InPostPL @RBrzoska https://t.co/F4AleTCViO — WNP.PL (@wnppl) August 18, 2026 The group behind the deal says the aim is to help InPost continue its recent rapid expansion. The firm will retain its name, branding and Polish headquarters. Founder and CEO Rafał Brzoska will remain in place, as well as being a major shareholder through A&R, which is his investment vehicle. The deal will see Advent, an American private equity firm, and FedEx each hold 37% of InPost. A&R would have 16% and PPF, a Czech investment fund founded by the late billionaire Petr Kellner, 10%. Currently, PPF holds 28.75%, A&R 12.49%, and Advent 6.5%. The initial offer period for the consortium’s takeover was due to end on 27 July. However, on 22 July, it was extended until 18 September due to the fact that antitrust proceedings in the EU and Vietnam were still ongoing. In its announcement today of EU approval, InPost noted that it is still awaiting a green light from the Vietnam Competition Commission but expects a decision to be made by 8 September. Although the Polish company has no operations in Vietnam, FedEx has been present on the market since 1994. InPost has grown rapidly in recent years through its pioneering use of parcel lockers, first in Poland and then across western Europe. In the UK, it has established a network of over 14,000 parcel lockers, including in branches of the British Post Office. In June this year, French President Emannuel Macron thanked InPost for its latest investment in France, where the firm – which operates there through its subsidiary Mondial Relay – is planning to spend a further €500 million to expand its presence. In the first quarter of 2026, InPost saw its revenue rise 31% year-on-year to reach 3.9 billion zloty. That included 121% growth in the UK, 28% in the Eurozone and 9% in Poland itself. However, the group’s earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA), a measure of profitability of business operations, were down 4% to 902 million zloty. World.title: Twelve killed as Polish coach crashes in Hungary
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Twelve people have died after a bus carrying Polish pilgrims from Medjugorje in Bosnia and Herzegovina back to Poland crashed on a motorway in Hungary. Initial findings indicate that the cause of the accident was the driver of the coach falling asleep. Political leaders in both Poland and Hungary have offered condolences to the families of the victims, while the Polish foreign ministry has set up a special helpline for those affected. BREAKING: 12 people have been killed after a Polish tourist bus crashed on a motorway in Hungary https://t.co/PAiZ4D1jU3 📺 Sky 501, Virgin 602, Freeview 233 and YouTube pic.twitter.com/yxW9tBN5bw — Sky News (@SkyNews) August 16, 2026 The accident occurred at around 1 a.m. local time on the night of Saturday to Sunday on the M3 motorway in Hungary. Later on Sunday morning, Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar confirmed that 12 people had died and at least 10 were seriously injured. According to information from the Hungarian emergency services, 57 passengers and two drivers had been on the bus. “The driver probably fell asleep at the wheel”, resulting in the vehicle veering off the road and into a ditch, said police in a statement quoted by Polsat News. Polsat reports that the group is from around Strzyżów, a town in southeastern Poland. The owner of the local company that had been transporting them told Business Insider Polska that the coach “was driven by two experienced drivers”. Twelve people lost their lives and at least ten were seriously injured overnight when a bus carrying Polish tourists overturned and went off the road into a ditch on the M3 motorway. Polish foreign ministry spokesman Maciej Wewiór later confirmed to broadcaster TVN that “everything indicates they were returning from Medjugorje”. The authorities in Podkarpackie, the province of Poland where the group was from, also reported that they were pilgrims returning from Bosnia and Herzegovina. The accident on Sunday morning took place just after the end of celebrations of the Assumption of Mary on Saturday, which had included the unveiling in Poland of Europe’s tallest statue of Mary. Andrii Sybiha, the foreign minister of Ukraine, which borders both Poland and Hungary, also offered his “heartfelt condolences” and said that “Ukraine stands in solidarity with the friendly Polish people and shares their grief”. World.title: Europe’s biggest Virgin Mary statue – taller than Rio’s Christ the Redeemer – unveiled in Polish village
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The tallest statue of the Virgin Mary in Europe has been officially opened in the small village of Konotopie in central Poland. Towering over the rural landscape at 55.6 metres high, the monument, whose construction was funded by a wealthy local couple, is taller than the famous Christ the Redeemer statue in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The new landmark, which is also the tallest religious statue of any kind in Europe, was unveiled on 15 August, when Catholics celebrate the assumption of Mary into heaven. The consecration ceremony was led by Krzysztof Wętkowski, bishop of the diocese of Włocławek in which Konotopie, which has a population of only around 130 people, is located. The local community hopes that the statue will become a major site of pilgrimage. Among those to attend the ceremony was former Polish president and Nobel Peace Prize winner Lech Wałęsa. “We sinners ask Our Lady of Mercy to take care of the whole nation,” wrote the 82-year-old in a post on social media, sharing photos of himself at the statue. Construction of the concrete statue took 18 months and reportedly cost around 100 million zloty (€23.2 million). Those costs were covered by the couple behind the project, Roman and Grażyna Karkosik. After making his fortune investing in undervalued companies during Poland’s post-communist transition in the 1990s, Roman Karkosik had by the early 21st century become one of Poland’s richest people, though his fortune has since diminished somewhat, according to estimates. The couple – who keep an extremely low profile, rarely giving interviews and never speaking publicly about the project to build the statue of Mary – live in a restored 18th-century palace around 2 kilometres away, from where they can see the new monument. Konotopie’s statue of Mary has now overtaken one in Miribel, France, as Europe’s tallest. But it is still some distance behind the tallest in the world, the 98-metre Mother of All Asia–Tower of Peace in Batangas City, Philippines. Until recently, Poland also had the tallest statue of Jesus in the world, the 33-metre-high Jesus Christ the King of the Universe monument, erected in the town of Świebodzin in 2010. However, in 2024, it was overtaken by a 61-metre-tall statue of Jesus in Indonesia. The design for the statue of Mary in Konotopie was originally conceived in the form of a two-metre-high model by sculptor Adam Jakub Matejkowski, who told the Polish edition of Forbes magazine that the Karkosiks had specifically requested that the statue be larger than Świebodzin’s Christ. Chief engineer Bartłomiej Niesłuchowski told broadcaster TVN that it took months to find a company willing and able to undertake such a project. Because no suppliers in Poland could produce the material needed for the unique mould into which the concrete would be poured, it had to be manufactured in Italy. The monument will be free for the public to access, including its observation deck, located 15 metres up on the pedestal upon which Mary stands. The site is expected to become a place of pilgrimage, with local authorities preparing for an influx of people. “We’re already seeing growing interest in investment plots, including restaurants,” Renata Gołębiewska, mayor of the nearby town of Kikoł, told the Rzeczpospolita daily. “But it’s too early to assess the impact.” Poland is one of Europe’s most religious countries. Just over 70% of the population identify as Catholic, according to the most recent national census, while around 30% attend Sunday mass. However, religiosity has been falling rapidly in recent years, especially among young Poles. The Catholic church in Poland has also been hit by a series of scandals relating to historical child sex abuse as well as accusations that it interferes in politics. The proportion of Catholics who attend Sunday mass in Poland has stabilised at around 30% after falling from a peak of 57%, new church data show.
