World.title: Convicted former Georgian PM Garibashvili: ‘Authorities left me no choice, I have to fight’
World.content:
Letter from Georgia’s former prime minister from prison

Convicted former Georgian prime minister Irakli Garibashvili says in a letter published from prison that the authorities arrested him to end his political career. He also says he gave up his legal fight to avoid a confrontation with the authorities.

The former prime minister writes that he received a letter from Regional Development Minister Mamuka Mdinaradze in July. According to Garibashvili, he confirmed to Mdinaradze that same day that he did not intend to return to politics.

Mamuka Mdinaradze’s press office has described Garibashvili’s claims as “complete absurdity”.

“I state with full responsibility that I did everything to avoid confrontation with the [ruling] team and with someone who is dear to me,” Garibashvili wrote.

He says this is why he abandoned his legal challenge and went through the entire process to the end — to avoid, as he put it, harming the interests of the state and the “team”.

“Unfortunately, in response I received a staged dirty provocation, a sea of lies and injustice. Throughout this time, the public heard not a single word from me. I endured this ordeal patiently,” Garibashvili said.

According to Garibashvili, despite the position he had expressed to Mdinaradze, the authorities believed there was still a “1% risk” that he might return to politics in the future.

“To avoid this, they wanted me to face corruption charges and admit guilt,” Garibashvili writes.

According to him, this demand became a “red line” that forced him to take the “most difficult step of my life” — to turn against the authorities.

“I have no other choice. I am forced to start fighting,” the former prime minister said.

On 17 August 2026, Garibashvili made his first public statement from prison. In a Facebook post, he said he had received an ultimatum in a letter sent on the instructions of Bidzina Ivanishvili. He added that he had “no other choice” but to stand against what he described as “evil that insults my dignity”.

“I tried to do everything possible to avoid taking this step, but unfortunately I have no other choice but to confront this evil that insults my dignity. I must confront this ruthless cruelty, oppression and injustice, as well as the dirty plan to destroy me and my family,” Garibashvili wrote.

He also said that Bidzina Ivanishvili and the government bear responsibility for the safety of both himself and his family.

In the letter, Garibashvili says he had remained publicly silent and patiently endured what was happening until now. However, he says the current situation has left him no choice but to begin fighting.

Letter from Georgia’s former prime minister from prison

World.title: Armenian prime minister’s wife launches campaign against domestic violence
World.content:
Anna Hakobyan’s campaign against domestic violence

The wife of Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan, Anna Hakobyan, has announced the launch of a campaign against domestic violence. She received death threats shortly after calling for a public discussion of the issue. However, she continues to actively promote her initiative.

“The first stage will involve drafting comprehensive and effective legislation and discussing it in the National Assembly,” she said.

According to Anna Hakobyan, the Criminal Code should define domestic violence separately as “a distinct and independent crime”. She plans to invite female MPs from the parliament’s two opposition factions to join her initiative. If they do, she believes there is a chance that “parliament will unanimously approve the bill”.

Anna Hakobyan calls for a “family model with no place for violence”

The prime minister’s wife posted a video message on social media in which she said she intended to continue fighting domestic violence. According to Hakobyan, Armenia’s traditional family model, which hides various forms of violence, should give way to a model of a “family with no place for violence, based on mutual love and respect”. She proposes amending the Criminal Code to achieve this goal:

“An individual article should be added to the Code to establish criminal liability for all forms of domestic violence. Alternatively, different chapters of the Code could include provisions covering specific forms of domestic violence, including beatings, psychological abuse, economic abuse, bodily harm, sexual violence and others.”

According to Anna Hakobyan, eradicating violence requires clear, realistic and effective legal mechanisms.

Before presenting the bill to parliament, she initiated discussions with independent experts and female MPs. Together, they plan to examine gaps in the existing legislation. Once the law comes into force, she has promised to launch the initiative’s second stage. This will involve:

organising an awareness campaign;

improving the skills of staff at relevant agencies;

ensuring the effective implementation of the new regulations.

“At the same time, a group of respected experts is preparing a nationwide study to collect the most accurate and comprehensive data possible on the prevalence of domestic violence against women in Armenia,” she said.

What preceded the campaign

This is not the prime minister’s wife’s first post about domestic violence. She has been actively raising the issue on her social media pages. At the end of July, she said she had received threats after a particular post, including threats to kill her.

“I hope the state authorities can prevent such a development, as it would seriously damage the country’s reputation if the prime minister’s wife became a victim of violence,” Hakobyan said.

At the same time, she urged women to overcome their fears and report cases of violence.

The Prosecutor General’s Office took note of her report. The Investigative Committee said it had opened a criminal case under the article on “hooliganism using information and communication technologies”.

“In addition, within the framework of another criminal case concerning public calls for violence, a warrant has been issued for the arrest of one person. The person has been placed on the wanted list,” Investigative Committee spokeswoman Kim Avdalyan said.

Statistics on domestic violence

The Investigative Committee said it opened 1,794 criminal cases related to domestic violence in the first half of 2026:

712 cases carried over from 2025;

1,082 cases opened in 2026.

Authorities sent 204 criminal cases to court and charged 213 people.

Of the 213 defendants in the cases sent to court, 150 were spouses of the victims, 20 were partners, 15 were parents or grandparents, five were brothers or sisters, 16 were children or grandchildren, one was the husband’s sister or brother, and six were sons- or daughters-in-law.

Of the 213 victims, 192 were over 18, while the rest were minors. Of those, 13 were under 12, three were aged 13-14, and five were aged 15-18.

Anna Hakobyan’s campaign against domestic violence

World.title: ‘Work is being carried out to international standards’ — Georgia’s Gelati Monastery Rehabilitation Committee responds to criticism
World.content:
Restoration of Georgia’s Gelati Monastery

The Temporary Committee for the Rehabilitation of Gelati has described reports circulating on social media and in the media about conservation work at the monastery as disinformation.

The committee said the disinformation was harming efforts to restore Gelati.

The Gelati Monastery complex is one of Georgia’s most important medieval cultural and religious monuments. King David IV, known as David the Builder, founded it in 1106.

The complex’s main church is the Cathedral of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary. In medieval Georgia, Gelati was not only a monastery but also an important centre of education and scholarship, home to the renowned Gelati Academy.

Recent reports and assessments have raised concerns about the condition of Gelati. The debate has focused on several issues:

The church’s temporary roof, which critics have called “cellophane”;

The risk of frescoes collapsing;

Mould and condensation inside the church;

The condition of the drainage system;

Plans to install an underfloor heating system;

Cooperation with the Italian institute Opificio delle Pietre Dure;

The condition of the mosaics at Gelati.

What does the committee say?

The committee rejects claims that the Gelati Cathedral is covered with “cellophane”. According to the committee, the creation of a single temporary covering for the cathedral was one of the main requirements set by the UNESCO World Heritage Centre as early as 2020.

The committee says Georgian and German specialists jointly designed the roof. The authorities approved the project after considering several proposals. The covering uses a high-tech PVC-based material made in Germany specifically for Gelati. According to the committee, the material meets international conservation standards.

The committee also rejects reports of widespread loss of frescoes inside the cathedral. It says all critically damaged areas have been stabilised, while conservation work on the wall paintings is continuing in stages.

The statement also addresses Gelati’s historic drainage system. According to the committee, drainage channels built during the reign of David the Builder stopped functioning in 1510 after Ottoman forces burned the monastery. The committee says archaeological excavations also support this conclusion.

“For centuries, the drainage system was filled with earth, ash and coal,” the committee said.

The committee also responded to criticism over humidity and condensation inside the church. According to the committee, Italian professor Dario Camuffo conducted the study of Gelati’s microclimate. The committee considers him one of the recognised experts in the study of the microclimate of cultural heritage sites.

The committee explained that the problem at Gelati stems from the church’s massive walls, which retain the cold for a long time during winter. In spring, when outdoor temperatures rise and warm air enters the church, condensation can form on the walls and floor.

Camuffo suggested gradually heating the floor as one possible solution. However, the committee stressed that this remains a working hypothesis and requires further research before a final decision.

The committee also clarified the memorandum it signed with the Italian institute Opificio delle Pietre Dure. According to the committee, the “pilot restoration” provided for in the document does not mean conducting experiments at Gelati. Instead, it refers to pilot or trial restoration work, which is standard international practice.

“This is a widely accepted standard for restoring wall paintings. Before treating an entire fresco, conservators test the safety of the proposed conservation methods on a small, less visible area. Only after obtaining a positive result do they begin the full-scale process,” the committee said.

In a significant part of its statement, the committee also responded to critics and addressed allegations about the condition of the mosaics at Gelati.

According to the committee, experts already knew about the poor condition of the mosaics in 1989. The claim is based on an assessment by restorer Carlo Bakuradze at the time, who found that about 85% of the mosaic depicting the Virgin Mary had detached from its base.

The committee also criticised specialists who question the ongoing conservation work and reminded them of their own responsibility for Gelati’s condition in the past.

“It is cynical and hypocritical for people to question the quality of conservation work when, under their direct supervision, extensive water-infiltration problems emerged within just one year at the recently built Bagrati Cathedral — problems that persist to this day,” the statement said. The Temporary Committee for the Rehabilitation of Gelati urged critics not to try to damage the reputation of the ongoing work and to act according to professional ethics.

“We call on those pursuing certain subjective goals and agendas to refrain from attempts to discredit the conservation work carried out under the Gelati rehabilitation programme and deliberately mislead the public. We also call on them to return to the standards of common decency and professional ethics,” the committee said.

The committee concluded by stressing again that the work at the Gelati Monastery complex is unprecedented in scale, involves international experts and meets international conservation standards.

What happened at Gelati?

The main problem at Gelati Monastery is water and dampness, which have damaged the church’s wall paintings and mosaics over time. The situation became particularly serious after restoration work in recent years, including problems with the roof.

The problem became so serious that the UNESCO World Heritage Centre and its advisory bodies issued specific recommendations to Georgia. The authorities changed their approach to the restoration work in response to those recommendations and established the current Rehabilitation Committee.

A ruling by Georgia’s Supreme Court also notes that workers carried out roofing work at Gelati without an adequate expert assessment. The court found that problems with the materials used and the quality of the installation created a real risk of water entering the building.

Restoration of Georgia’s Gelati Monastery

World.title: Suicides in Armenia’s military: the statistics and debate over who should be held responsible
World.content:
Suicides in Armenia’s army: statistics

In Armenia, debate continues over the causes of military deaths in peacetime and who should bear responsibility. A series of suicides has prompted the latest discussions. The first incident occurred on 21 July. Then, on 13 August, the Defence Ministry reported that it had found the body of serviceman Grigor Zakaryan with a gunshot wound. In both cases, the Investigative Committee said it had opened criminal proceedings under the article on negligent incitement to suicide.

According to the Vanadzor office of the Helsinki Citizens’ Assembly, this was the 31st military death in Armenia in 2026. However, the Defence Ministry says 11 servicemen have died. Moreover, the ministry’s spokesperson said the number of military deaths had become the subject of various forms of manipulation.

“We often see reports in the press about 30 deaths in the army over the course of a year. But no one says how many of those 30 cases actually occurred in the army, which were related to military service and which were not. Even if the deaths were related to service, were all of them murders and suicides?” Aram Torosyan said, calling for greater precision.

Government bodies and civil society organisations also differ over who should bear responsibility for military deaths. Human rights groups tend to argue that the defence minister and the chief of the General Staff should be held accountable. However, Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan does not share this view.

“In my assessment, it is not the case that the chief of the General Staff and the defence minister are failing to make sufficient efforts to address this issue,” Nikol Pashinyan said.

Civil society data differs from official figures

Human rights activist Nazeli Movsesyan, who represents the Vanadzor office of the Helsinki Citizens’ Assembly, said she had seen no positive changes. According to her, the number of military deaths in non-combat situations has not decreased:

“The situation is even worse than in 2025. There were 35 deaths throughout 2025, while there have already been 31 cases in the first eight months of this year.”

She stressed that 10 cases in 2025 were classified as related to military service, while the same number have been recorded in just eight months this year.

Defence Ministry spokesman Aram Torosyan says these claims do not match the official statistics.

“We have recorded 11 deaths this year. Only five of those who died were serving their mandatory military service. Some died from illness, while others died in a mine explosion,” he said.

Torosyan said six of the 11 deaths involved suicide or incitement to suicide, but only three were related to military service.

Commenting on last year’s figures, he stressed that there were no cases of murder in the army in 2025.

Causes of suicides in the army

The authorities have not released details about the death of serviceman Grigor Zakaryan. However, the prime minister said that 85-90% of suicides in the army result from:

gambling addiction and the debts it causes;

personal and family problems;

servicemen falling asleep while on duty, which can lead to conflicts with fellow soldiers.

“If a serviceman on duty at a border post falls asleep, he puts other people’s lives at risk. Soldiers then begin to treat the person who fell asleep at the post negatively, and he becomes isolated. After returning from combat duty, psychological pressure can also follow. We should not place all the blame on the army leadership. I am responsible for the fact that we have still not found a solution to this problem,” Pashinyan said.

Human rights activist Nazeli Movsesyan believes that the first two causes mentioned by the prime minister have nothing to do with the army. At the same time, she believes authorities can eliminate the third factor by taking systemic measures:

“Why does a serviceman fall asleep while on duty? Are there enough personnel to ensure that everyone gets enough rest and does not feel the need to sleep while on duty?”

Prime minister’s statements and dismissals

On the day the soldier died, Nikol Pashinyan told reporters that the government had discussed the situation and decided to make dismissals. He announced personnel changes in the Military Police and the Defence Ministry’s Department of Moral and Psychological Support:

“We will analyse in detail why our efforts in this area are not producing the desired results and draw conclusions. Yes, there must be individual accountability.”

The same day, reports emerged that Military Police chief Ashot Zakaryan had submitted his resignation. Today, the president dismissed Zakaryan from the post he had held for six years. In another decree, Major General Aram Hovhannisyan was appointed to replace him. From 2023 to 2025, he served as deputy interior minister and police chief.

There are no specific details yet about personnel changes in the Department of Moral and Psychological Support.

In recent days, the Defence Ministry has reported consultations on organising psychological support in the armed forces. To review a report on the psychological assistance provided to the military, the defence minister met professors from Yerevan State University’s Research Centre for Psychology. The ministry is also holding discussions with conscript sergeants and officers serving on duty at military posts.

“The agenda includes issues related to preventing hazing and eliminating inappropriate behaviour in the army,” the ministry said.

Comment

Human rights activist Zhanna Aleksanyan believes:

“The army’s top command, led by Suren Papikyan, must give the public a detailed explanation of the series of deaths.

Has anyone from the army’s top command visited the military unit to establish the circumstances of the soldier’s death and find out what was happening there? I strongly doubt it.

Papikyan did not even visit the military unit in the village of Azat when 15 servicemen died.

On 19 January 2023, a fire broke out in the engineering and sapper company’s premises in the village of Azat, killing 15 servicemen. Three others suffered burns of varying severity.

Then, as now, Nikol Pashinyan spoke on Papikyan’s behalf. He named those responsible and accountable. But he did not explain what the Military Police had to do with the death.

If Pashinyan knows more about the situation in the army and at military units, why is Papikyan still the defence minister?”

Suicides in Armenia’s army: statistics

World.title: Azerbaijani Ukrainian Congress denounces calls by some Russian media outlets
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. The Congress of Azerbaijanis in Ukraine strongly condemned statements made by representatives of certain Russian media outlets that called for the disintegration of Azerbaijan, the carrying out of terrorist acts on the territory of Azerbaijan, and other unlawful actions aimed at violating the territorial integrity of the state.

This was announced by Congress on its social media account.

Meanwhile, it is reported that criminal proceedings have been initiated by Azerbaijani law enforcement authorities against these experts, and they have been placed on an international wanted list.

In addition, it is noted that the Ambassador of the Russian Federation was summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Azerbaijan and was firmly informed that such conduct is unacceptable.

The Azerbaijan-Ukraine Congress announced that it considers the measures taken against the experts who made offensive statements about our Motherland to be entirely reasonable and appropriate.

World.title: Azerbaijani journalists visit Imam al-Bukhari tourist complex near Samarkand (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. On August 20, as part of a press tour to Uzbekistan, Azerbaijani journalists visited the Imam al-Bukhari tourist complex, located near Samarkand.

Twenty representatives from Azerbaijan’s leading media outlets are participating in the press tour. Among the participants is Emin Aliyev, editor-in-chief of the Trend International News Agency.

The press tour participants toured the modern complex, created to study and promote the scholarly legacy of the outstanding Islamic scholar and one of the most renowned hadith scholars, Imam Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari (810–870).

The journalists paid particular attention to the architectural features and modern infrastructure of the complex, which was built to accommodate pilgrims and foreign tourists. Specifically, the complex includes a mosque with a capacity of up to 10,000 worshippers, four minarets 75 meters high, and a museum complex consisting of nine pavilions.

During the tour, representatives of the Azerbaijani media received information about the life and scholarly work of Imam al-Bukhari, his contribution to Islamic theology, and the significance of his seminal work, ''Sahih al-Bukhari'', considered one of the most authoritative collections of hadiths in the Sunni Islamic tradition.

At the meeting, it was noted that following a large-scale renovation, the complex has become a major spiritual, educational, and tourist center. The complex now offers facilities not only for pilgrimage but also for the study of Islamic cultural and scientific heritage.

As part of the project, hotels, family guesthouses, service areas, and parking lots have also been built. The complex’s capacity has been increased to 65,000 visitors per day.

A visit to the Imam al-Bukhari Complex was one of the stops on a press tour aimed at familiarizing representatives of the Azerbaijani media with Uzbekistan’s historical, cultural, tourist, and modern potential.

World.title: Uzbekistan’s Fergana, China’s Guohong eye new logistics center
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Uzbekistan’s Fergana region and China’s Guohong Trade Development Group are considering the creation of a new logistics center as part of efforts to expand trade and economic cooperation.

This was reflected in the statement by the Fergana Regional Administration, following a meeting between Governor Khayrullo Bozorov and Gui Yan, director and general manager of Guohong Trade Development Group.

According to the Regional Administration, the proposed logistics center could strengthen Fergana’s transport and supply-chain infrastructure and support greater trade flows between Uzbekistan, China and other international markets.

Meanwhile, the meeting highlighted the dynamic development of trade and economic ties between Uzbekistan and China and focused on opportunities to launch joint projects in Fergana.

During the meeting, the sides put forward proposals to establish a manufacturing facility producing high-value-added products in Fergana, as well as a specialized training center for professionals in modern fields such as mechanical engineering and mechatronics.

The proposed training center could help develop local technical skills and provide businesses with qualified specialists for manufacturing and technology-intensive industries.

The sides agreed to develop a portfolio of prospective projects based on specific implementation plans and continue expanding cooperation through exchanges of business and official delegations.

The initiatives discussed during the meeting could contribute to industrial development, technology-oriented workforce training and the expansion of logistics capacity in Fergana, while creating new opportunities for Chinese companies to participate in investment projects in the region.

Guohong Trade Development Group operates in foreign trade, import and export, international freight transportation, logistics, and supply chain management. The company exports products to markets in Europe, the United States, Malaysia and other countries.

World.title: Azerbaijani MFA extends condolences to Central African Republic
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Azerbaijan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs has extended condolences to the Central African Republic following a fatal accident at a gold mine.

This was announced in a post published by the Azerbaijani MFA on its X account.

“We are deeply saddened by the news of a deadly gold mine accident in the Central African Republic, which claimed many lives and caused injuries.

We extend our heartfelt condolences to the families of the victims and to the people and government of the Central African Republic.

We wish the injured a swift and full recovery and hope that everyone affected is brought to safety as quickly as possible,” the statement said.

A mine collapse at a gold site near the border between Cameroon and the Central African Republic reportedly claimed the lives of around 100 people.

World.title: Iran claims U.S. shifts to economic pressure after military approach fails
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Iran says the United States has shifted its approach toward economic pressure after failing to achieve its goals through military means.

This was stated by Kazem Garibabadi, Iran's Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs for Legal and International Affairs, in a post on his official X page.

"The military war did not work; now they have named the next defeat 'economic war'," Gharibabadi wrote.

He accused Washington of making "miscalculations" and attempting to justify its policies by increasing pressure on Tehran. "They claim that Iran is on the verge of defeat and is hanging by a thread, but they are begging all their allies to help them," the Iranian deputy foreign minister stated.

Gharibabadi added that, in his view, the United States’ approach was based on incorrect assessments, which forced it to adopt increasingly tougher measures.

Earlier, US President Donald Trump, in his post on Truth Social, announced economic warfare and isolation towards Iran.

"No one has given the Islamic Republic of Iran a greater opportunity to make a Deal than me. Tragically, for them, they have failed to take it. Therefore, today, I am announcing the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country! This will be Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale. Their navy is gone, their air force is destroyed, their military factories are now rubble, their currency is worthless, and their country is hanging by a thread. Today, I am also announcing that any country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face tremendous Economic Consequences. Oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, front companies — it all needs to stop now. You know who you are. This will be an economic D-Day, and we need all of our Allies to stand with the United States of America to isolate and defeat the Iran threat. These maniacs are on the ropes, and these historic measures will cripple them and their ability to project terror worldwide. Iran will never have a nuclear weapon," Trump wrote.

World.title: Azerbaijan Airlines and ABB launch onboard POS payment capability
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Azerbaijan Airlines and ABB Bank, a lifestyle partner for its customers, have launched a new solution aimed at enhancing the passenger experience. Passengers can now pay for additional services onboard Azerbaijan Airlines aircraft using ABB POS terminals.

With this solution, passengers can quickly and securely pay by bank card for additional services available during the flight via ABB POS terminals.

As part of the new service, subject to availability, passengers can pay onboard for a more comfortable seat in Economy Class, as well as for an upgrade to Business Class or Premium Economy. This makes the process of accessing and paying for additional services more flexible and convenient.

The new solution is another step in the national carrier’s initiatives to enhance passenger experience and advance digital transformation. The airline continues to expand the use of digital solutions across various stages of the journey, increasing service accessibility and providing passengers with a wider range of choices.

For ABB Bank, the introduction of onboard POS payment is a continuation of its projects to develop new solutions tailored to customers every day and travel needs. As part of its lifestyle banking approach, ABB brings together diverse services on a single platform to meet customers’ needs both in their everyday lives and while travelling.

The new solution, implemented through cooperation between Azerbaijan Airlines and ABB Bank, enables passengers to conveniently access additional services during the flight and pay for them directly onboard, further enhancing the overall customer experience.

World.title: Uzbekistan’s Fergana, Russia's Rosatom set new priorities for joint projects
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, August 20. Uzbekistan’s Fergana region and Russia’s Rosatom have identified new areas for cooperation, including investment projects, production localization, nuclear medicine, energy storage and transport logistics.

This was reflected in the statement by the Fergana Regional Administration, following a meeting between Governor Khayrullo Bozorov and a delegation led by Alexey Dremuchev, director general of Rosatom’s representative office in Central Asia and Japan.

According to the Regional Administration, in the course of the meeting, the sides focused on mutually beneficial cooperation, prospective investment projects and the localization of production in the region.

Dremuchev outlined Rosatom’s activities across a broad range of sectors, including nuclear energy, mechanical engineering, nuclear medicine, energy, digital technologies and advanced materials production.

The meeting highlighted Fergana’s favorable investment environment and significant industrial potential as potential foundations for expanding cooperation with Rosatom.

The sides considered the possibility of launching a pilot project in healthcare, as well as joint initiatives in the fuel and energy sector, energy storage, composite materials production, workforce training and transport and logistics.

“Fergana is ready to support mutually beneficial initiatives and joint projects,” Bozorov said, according to the regional administration.

The proposed projects could broaden Rosatom’s cooperation with Uzbekistan beyond its traditional nuclear energy activities and create opportunities for technology transfer, industrial localization and workforce development in the region.

Particular attention was also given to production localization, which could help strengthen local manufacturing capabilities and increase the participation of Uzbek enterprises in projects involving Russian technology and expertise.

Following the meeting, the sides agreed to develop a Roadmap outlining priority areas of cooperation and joint projects, supported by a specific action plan.

The roadmap is expected to provide a framework for translating the agreements reached during the meeting into concrete investment and industrial initiatives in Fergana.

World.title: 'Do better': Albanese issues stern criticism of AFL in wake of Swans scandal
World.content:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has criticised the AFL over its handling of the current scandal engulfing the league.

On Wednesday, the Swans stood down five players for the rest of the AFL season — vice captain Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon, Riley Bice and Nick Blakey — for breaching club standards for drinking and bringing women to the hotel.

Police from Victoria's sexual crimes squad have since flown to New South Wales and are investigating report of sexual assault, which the ABC understands centres on a player allegedly touching one of the women without her consent.

Swans players James Jordon, Chad Warner, Isaac Heeney, Nick Blakey and Riley Bice have been stood down. (Getty Images/ABC News)

Mr Albanese told 7.30 that he felt the initial response was not good enough.

"It's extraordinary that this has occurred," Mr Albanese said.

"The idea that this is occurring is completely untenable, and the initial response as well was, I think, completely unacceptable.

"The NRL have a no-fault stand down clause for issues like this, but the first thoughts should have been always about women and their safety.

" I don't think that occurred at this time. The AFL certainly needs to do better. "

That initial response came on Monday afternoon when Swans CEO and Fremantle Dockers great Matthew Pavlich confirmed several players had been linked to the alleged incident.

Sydney Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich has issued several statements this week. (Getty Images: Mark Metcalfe)

"We’re still piecing together exactly what’s transpired here and have our own set of internal inquiries ongoing," Mr Pavlich said on Monday.

"But safe to say that we’re extremely shocked and disappointed that this has taken place and that the players have found themselves in this situation."

On Tuesday AFL CEO Andrew Dillon described the allegations as "deeply disturbing" in a statement.

On Thursday night the ABC reported that detectives investigating have been told some players paid female adult entertainers to consume drugs off their bodies.

Police have not made any arrests or laid charges.

Mr Albanese said the AFL and the Swans should "have a good look" at their culture.

Albanese to press Israel over Frankcom

While Mr Albanese was focused on several issues at home, the major geopolitical issue of the day involved Israel.

On Wednesday night, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) cleared its personnel of any criminal wrongdoing over a 2024 strike on a humanitarian convoy, which killed Australian woman Zomi Frankcom.

Ms Frankcom was killed in a strike by the IDF. (Supplied: Facebook)

The decision was described as an "outrage" by Foreign Minister Penny Wong on Thursday morning.

Mr Albanese told 7.30 he wanted a much more transparent response from the Israeli government.

"It clearly is an outrage and there's a need for a far more transparent and clear explanation from the Israeli government other than what we've received," Mr Albanese said.

Asked if that would involve an independent investigation, Mr Albanese said it was one option.

"It's certainly not good enough that on World Humanitarian Day ... they release this so-called report that essentially says, 'Yes, we're responsible, but nothing to see here', he said".

"Zomi represented the best of Australians out there in a dangerous area, helping her fellow global citizens as she had in other parts of the world that were suffering conflict as well. And that's why it deserves better.

"Her family deserved better, and frankly, Australia deserves better.

"We will press the Israeli government.

"[We] will discuss with Ms Frankcom's family. They deserve to be consulted on these issues and we'll do that, and then we'll make an announcement in coming days."

PM concedes podcast appearance was 'an error'

The Prime Minister was also asked about criticism he's faced over several comments he made on the Deep Bush podcast.

Loading...

Mr Albanese first came under scrutiny for playing "shag, marry, date" on the podcast, which was broadcast in July.

He has since unequivocally apologised for saying he would "shag" Kylie Minogue.

Recently it was hand gestures he made on the podcast, while referring to a pair of melons given to him by Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae, that caused controversy.

Mr Albanese has not apologised specifically for the melon interaction and maintains that the gestures have been misinterpreted.

Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. (Reuters: Hollie Adams)

However, he told 7.3 that in hindsight he should not have gone on the podcast and that he had learned from it.

"I learned that I need to do better every day," Mr Albanese said.

"If I had my time again ... then I wouldn't have done that podcast.

" We have a view which is trying to talk to as many people as possible, but clearly that was an error. "

Watch 7.30, Mondays to Thursdays 7:30pm on ABC iview and ABC TV

World.title: Zomi Frankcom's family 'deeply disappointed' IDF won't pursue charges
World.content:
The family of Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom, who was killed in an Israeli strike while delivering humanitarian aid in Gaza in 2024, has slammed the Israeli military's decision not to pursue criminal charges against the commanders who ordered the attack.

The statement, issued by Zomi's brother Mal on behalf of the Frankcom family, said family members were "deeply disappointed" by the decision, having spent the past two years waiting for justice while "hoping and calling for an independent criminal investigation".

"Zomi and her colleagues deserve more than an internal, opaque process that ends with a short statement by the Israeli military absolving their soldiers of criminal wrongdoing," they said.

" The families of the victims deserve transparency and an independent judicial assessment of the criminal responsibility for the international humanitarian law violations that took place on that day. "

Ms Frankcom was one of seven World Central Kitchen aid workers killed on April 1, 2024, while taking part in a convoy helping to deliver food and other supplies to northern Gaza.

The group was travelling in three armoured cars branded with the World Central Kitchen logo, and driving through part of the Gaza Strip that had been declared a "humanitarian fire control zone" while coordinating movements with the IDF (Israel Defense Forces).

An Israeli drone fired three missiles at the convoy — one at each of the cars in succession — as survivors of the initial strike attempted to move from one vehicle to another.

Wreckage of one of three World Central Kitchen vehicles destroyed in the strikes. (Reuters: Ahmed Zakot)

An Australian investigation into the Israeli government's response to the incident, led by retired defence chief Air Chief Marshal Mark Binskin, found the deaths had been the result of the first vehicle being misidentified due to a number of factors, including the presence of armed security in the vicinity, confirmation bias and a "failure within the IDF to fully disseminate and/or read the detailed movement plan approved by the convoy".

Wong declares 'difficult time' in relations with Israel Foreign Minister Penny Wong says she has "no confidence" in the IDF investigation that cleared Israeli soldiers of criminal wrongdoing.

The subsequent strikes were also found to be a breach of IDF procedures and the rules of engagement, echoing the findings of a rapid FFAM ("fact-finding and assessment mechanism") investigation conducted by the IDF in the days following the incident.

Two IDF officers were fired in the weeks after the strikes, while others were reprimanded.

In their statement released on Thursday evening, Ms Frankcom's family expressed disagreement with the finding that there was no wrongdoing involved that merited at least a criminal investigation, highlighting the follow-up strikes as well as the fact that one of the officers involved had reportedly signed a letter earlier that year calling for the flow of aid to Gaza to be restricted.

They also expressed outrage at the timing of the announcement, which came on World Humanitarian Day, an internationally recognised day dedicated to those who have died working for humanitarian causes.

A humanitarian award has since been created in Ms Frankcom's name. (Supplied: X)

The family had been standing alongside Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong at an event at Parliament House just hours prior to the announcement, launching a humanitarian award in Ms Frankcom's name.

"For it to be announced on World Humanitarian Day, the day the world pauses to remember those who have lost their lives while helping others … is an insult to my sister's memory," Ms Frankcom's brother Mal said.

Senator Wong similarly expressed anger at the announcement, saying she had no confidence in the IDF's findings, and calling in Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, to explain the decision.

Calling today's events a "difficult time" in diplomatic relations with Israel, she said she was informed of the IDF's decision just minutes before it was publicly announced, and did not have time to alert Ms Frankcom's family.

World.title: Proposed gun reforms 'betrayal of Tasmanians', critics say
World.content:
The Tasmanian government's watered-down gun law reforms have been described as "extraordinarily weak" and a "betrayal of Tasmanians" by Labor and the Greens.

The proposed reforms, which were tabled in state parliament on Thursday, were a response to calls to tighten gun laws in the wake of last year's Bondi terror attack.

But gun control advocates say the legislation tabled today is even "weaker" than the much-criticised draft legislation released earlier this year.

The bill still does not include a limit on the number of guns one person can own, despite the state's Police Commissioner Donna Adams calling for it.

It still reclassifies straight pull and button or lever release shotguns to the more restrictive Category C and introduces an Australian citizenship requirement for owners, with carve-outs for New Zealand citizens and people who need them for work.

But it now grandfathers these clauses, meaning the rules do not apply to guns that people already own or to non-citizens who currently own legal guns.

One gun advocate says "law-abiding firearms owners probably aren't going to be too happy" with the reforms. (ABC News)

Greens' police spokesperson Tabatha Badger said the bill was "deeply disappointing" and "simply not good enough".

"Tasmanians expected so much more when it came to firearm safety in this state," she said.

"We'd already seen a draft bill out for public consultation that was underwhelming, and what we've seen today tabled in this parliament is an incredible disappointment.

"It's very clear that this police minister does not understand that public safety is a core part of his job."

Tabatha Badger says the government should be "incredibly ashamed" of its proposal. (ABC News: Luke Bowden)

Ms Badger cited the Port Arthur shootings of 1996 and raised concerns about the grandfathering of clauses, the decision to include changes to antique gun laws and the addition of mandatory minimum sentences for stolen firearms.

"This Liberal government should be incredibly ashamed of what they have put forward," she said.

"Tasmania was a state that, in the past, has led the way off the back of incredible tragedy to reform firearms to help make our community safer. In the years that have followed, we simply haven't kept up with that."

What we know about guns in Australia Gun control researchers say we have "no idea" how many black market and 3D-printed weapons are out there.

Labor leader Josh Willie accused the government of being "soft on crime".

"This is a betrayal of Tasmanians and community safety by Premier Rockliff," he said.

"He has a position to support unlimited guns.

" He's backflipped on his position to improve community safety and I think, rightly, Tasmanians will be questioning whether he's got their back. "

Bill defended by police minister

The bill also follows through on a 2024 election promise of no licence requirements for antique firearms.

Antique firearms manufactured before January 1, 1900 will only have to be registered with Tasmania Police.

Police Minister Felix Ellis said the legislation strikes the right balance and will result in a significant uplift in community safety.

Police Minister Felix Ellis has defended the changes, saying Tasmanians will be safer as a result of the reforms. (Facebook: Felix Ellis)

He defended the grandfathered clauses, saying they were about "ensuring that the transition is right".

"That we can continue to support people who are farmers, hunters and recreational shooters who have been complying with the law," he said.

"We had people who have lived here for decades, who are not citizens of Australia, but have complied with our laws here in Tasmania when it comes to their firearms and [are of] good character, so rather than unduly penalising those people, it allows us to establish a framework moving forward."

Mr Ellis also said the mandatory minimum sentences for stolen firearms were particularly important.

"It'll ensure that if you steal a firearm or you're caught in possession of a stolen firearm you will go to jail," he said.

"That is absolutely vital so we can ensure that illegal firearms are not being used to intimidate our community and aren't being used to fuel organised crime."

An agreement to reclassify guns has been grandfathered, prompting backlash. (ABC News)

The bill will support the implementation of the National Firearms Register in the state, which the minister said would improve intelligence sharing between law enforcement and intelligence agencies.

"We've seen that the failures of Bondi have been very much about the failure to share intelligence, particularly about people who are seeking to do harm in the community," Mr Ellis said.

"So this uplift will be critical."

Opposition to push amendments

Gun Control Australia vice president Roland Browne accused the Tasmanian government of going sideways and backwards.

"The agreement reached in December required reclassification of guns and Tasmania has done that, but then they've grandfathered the clauses that make those reclassification decisions operative.

"In other words, if people are going to have their guns reclassified … shooters in Tasmania keep their guns.

" How is that going to make Tasmania a safer place? "

Roland Browne questions the efficacy of the proposed reforms. (ABC News: Monty Jacka)

But nor were gun advocates satisfied.

In a social media video, Tasmanian Shooters Union President Phillip Bigg said it didn't seem like their consultations were taken note of.

"Law-abiding firearms owners probably aren't going to be too happy," he said.

"I've had a quick look, doesn't look very good."

Mr Bigg also acknowledged that Labor and the Greens were likely to try to make their own amendments to the bill.

That was confirmed by both parties today, with Mr Willie telling the media the party is still intent on introducing caps on guns.

"We've said consistently we'll promote community safety while respecting the legitimate ownership of legal firearms owners," he said.

"We'll work with the parliament around amendments. We're committed to doing that."

Phillip Bigg says the Tasmanian Shooters Union would work with parliament on the amendments. (ABC News)

The two parties combined will need to find another four votes to get any amendments through the lower house.

The state government said there will be a six-month voluntary buyback scheme that will begin once the bill has royal assent.

It is still in negotiations with the federal government about the cost.

Parliament is set to debate the bill in the first week of September.

World.title: Max Verstappen signs to stay with Red Bull F1
World.content:
Max Verstappen has ended speculation over his Formula 1 future by signing a contract extension that will see him remain at Red Bull Racing until 2030.

The four-time world champion has repeatedly threatened to walk away from F1 this season in protest at the new power unit in use.

Red Bull have struggled with the regulations this year, with Verstappen's best performances two second-place finishes in Austria and Hungary.

Verstappen sits in sixth place in the drivers' standings this season without a win through the first 11 grands prix.

The Dutch star, who finished just two points behind world champion Lando Norris last season, was previously contracted to the end of 2028.

However, there were clauses in his contract that could have allowed him to leave at the end of the season.

The Red Bull team have struggled under the new regulations. (Getty Images: PA Images/David Davies)

The 28-year-old was linked with potential moves to Mercedes and McLaren, involving an outlandish driver swap with Australian Oscar Piastri; however, he will now stay at the team with whom he has won 71 grands prix.

"I am really pleased with the contract extension," Verstappen said in a statement.

"We have the best people, and I'm excited to keep working together with everyone to get back to the top again.

"This remains the ultimate goal that all of us have been working towards and will continue to pursue. I want to thank Red Bull, Laurent [Mekies] and everyone at Oracle Red Bull Racing for the trust they put in me."

The F1 season has just finished its summer break, with racing to resume at Verstappen's home Dutch Grand Prix this weekend at Zandvoort, the last time the circuit will be on the calendar.

"To make this announcement during the last Grand Prix at Zandvoort is a great moment for me as well," Verstappen said.

"Hopefully we can give the fans a special send-off for the final race."

Verstappen won the first two Dutch Grand Prix upon the race's return to F1 in 2021, but has been beaten into second place the last two seasons, by Norris in 2024 and Piastri last season.

"I have always said it, the team is like a second family for me, and I feel very at home," Verstappen said.

"I came to the team hoping to be able to win races. What we went on to achieve together has been simply lovely.

"To continue this journey with the same team that I have been with my whole career is really special and something I have always wanted to do."

Max Verstappen will be racing in F1 until 2030 after signing a new contract. (Getty Images: Marcel van Dorst/EYE4IMAGES/NurPhoto)

Verstappen joined the Red Bull Junior Programme in 2014 and, after starting 23 grands prix for Scuderia Toro Rosso, made his F1 debut with the full Red Bull team midway through the 2016 season as a replacement for Daniil Kvyat.

The then-teenage star claimed a stunning victory in that race, becoming the youngest-ever grand prix winner aged 18 years and 228 days.

"Having Max continue with us and retaining the best driver on the grid is fantastic news for everyone at Red Bull, Oracle Red Bull Racing, as well as F1 and motorsport as a whole," Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said.

"Very few partnerships in sport achieve what Max and this team have.

"His impact on our team and on Red Bull's motorsport story has been transformational, and he has been fundamental to everything we have accomplished together.

"But we are not done yet. There are more races to win, more milestones to achieve and more history to write."

Red Bull has already had to deal with some disruption in the mid-season shutdown, with Isack Hadjar suffering a wrist injury that will rule him out of the Dutch Grand Prix.

New Zealander Liam Lawson will step up and take Hadjar's seat, with test driver Yuki Tsunoda taking the Kiwi's Racing Bulls seat for the round.

World.title: Driver waits for compensation after new EV suddenly stops on freeway
World.content:
Prabin Gautam was travelling at 85 kilometres per hour on the Princes Freeway between Melbourne and Geelong when his electric vehicle sounded an alert and suddenly slowed to walking pace.

Then it stopped moving altogether.

"I thought, 'What's going on?'" Mr Gautam said.

For about seven minutes he was stuck in his XPeng G6 on the freeway, unable to get out as traffic streamed past.

"I was really freaked out," Mr Gautum said.

"I could not open the window. I could not open the door. I could not do anything and everyone is beeping at me.

" I just have to close my eyes and then I thought, 'OK, look, I'll have to try again.' "

After a few minutes he was able to slowly drive his car onto the side of the road.

"My hands were shaking and there were still a lot of errors coming through," Mr Gautam said.

When Mr Gautum eventually got hold of the company that sold him his XPeng, the news was not good.

It was a drive-motor problem.

Prabin Gautam only drives short distances after a frightening experience in it on a Victorian freeway. (ABC News: Jonathon Kendall)

"They knew about it in other cars by the sound of it," he said.

Mr Gautam bought the car in February 2025 for $64,000 from XPeng Port Melbourne, which was operated by TrueEV.

Since the incident in June, he has received the same error message twice and says he only feels confident to drive his car short distances on quiet roads.

Part of the attraction to the car was the offer of five years of free servicing, but that has not been available because of a legal dispute between XPeng and its former exclusive Australian distributor, TrueEV.

Mr Gautam spent weeks seeking a refund or replacement vehicle, but he said aside from a few noncommittal emails he has been ignored by both companies.

Many XPeng buyers were attracted by the cashback and servicing offers. (ABC News: Jonathon Kendall)

Left in the lurch

Mr Gautam is one of hundreds of customers and creditors left in the lurch after XPeng terminated its five-year distribution agreement with TrueEV at the start of the year.

TrueEV was placed into receivership in March and the two companies have been locked in a legal battle ever since.

The ABC has been contacted by 14 customers and creditors who say they have been left out of pocket by TrueEV.

Most say they are owed between $1,000 and $9,000, including many who have not receive the $5,000 cashback they were offered.

Cashback delays frustrate electric-vehicle owners When Mustansir Milky took the leap and bought a new electric vehicle, he didn't expect to have to fight to get the $5,000 cashback payment he was promised.

Some say they cannot get parts, have not received accessories they paid for, or have had to pay for their own servicing and want compensation.

TrueEV initially told the ABC it could answer questions about the situation after the resolution of its federal court case with XPeng, in which TrueEV was challenging the legality of XPeng's decision to cancel its five-year distribution deal.

That case was dismissed today after it was revealed TrueEV could not provide the required court surety.

"We are very disappointed with the outcome of today's judgement," True EV's Jason Clarke said in a statement.

"TrueEV will now review its options, including appeal or bringing a new case to trial.

"We will advise the market in due course."

XPeng recognised that some customers had "experienced frustration" and assured owners they would be looked after.

"Where an eligible cashback or extended warranty commitment made by TrueEV is appropriately documented and verified, XPeng ANZ is working directly with the customer to provide appropriate support," it said in a statement.

Creditors owed a lot more

Ultra Tune Australia was contracted to provide servicing and roadside assistance for XPeng customers who were promised five years of free services.

Ultra Tune national operations and business development manager Nick Tatsis said the company was owed more than $100,000.

"Unfortunately, we haven't been paid, so we've had to cease those operations till we find a solution," he said.

Nick Tatsis says his company is owed more than $100,000. (Supplied: Nick Tatsis)

That has meant XPeng owners have had to pay for servicing themselves and try to recoup that money from TrueEV or XPeng.

Mr Tatsis says his company paid for licensing and training for its franchisees about how to work on XPeng electric vehicles.

He said franchisees also set up servicing facilities at a considerable cost.

"It was a very hard call to make, because XPeng customers are our customers and we don't want to let them down," Mr Tatsis said.

"We don't want to say no in any instance, but we're not getting paid for the services and we've had no other choice."

Still waiting to be paid

Melbourne graphic designer Yibo Li was engaged by TrueEV to create marketing content for the XPeng brand in Australia between October last year and February this year.

He created visuals for the website and dealerships point of sale and worked on the $5,000 cashback campaign.

Yibo Li has been contacting TrueEV for the payment of $21,410 he says he's owed. (ABC News: Jonathon Kendall)

Li said he received $4,500 for his work but was owed a further $21,410.

The ABC has seen invoices sent to TrueEV for the detailing of a three-phase marketing campaign and the emails seeking payment.

"That's a significant amount of money for independent designer or small studio," he said.

Customer offers included $5,000 cashback and free servicing for five years. (ABC News: Jonathon Kendall)

Li said alarm bells started to ring in December last year when his invoices were not being paid.

"I actually feel sorry for those customers," he said.

World.title: Evergrande founder sentenced to life in prison by Chinese court
World.content:
Chinese property developer Hui Ka Yan, founder of the Evergrande real estate group, has been sentenced to life in prison with the companies fined a total of $US2.3 billion ($3.2 billion), by a court in the southern city of Shenzhen.

The decision marks a milestone in Evergrande's saga after it collapsed with more than $US300 billion ($420 billion) in liabilities when Chinese authorities cracked down on excessive borrowing in the real estate industry in 2020.

That triggered a crunch among many developers and brought on a downturn in the property market that has weighed on the broader economy ever since.

The Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court convicted Hui, also known as Xu Jiayin, and Evergrande of large-scale financial fraud in inflating the group's assets and concealing its liabilities.

Evergrande was fined $1.85 billion in addition to Hui's sentence. (Reuters: Aly Song)

In a statement, the court said Hui also abused his position in orchestrating financial fraud and misappropriating company assets.

Hui had faced eight charges including misuse of funds and illegally taking public deposits.

It also sentenced several other senior Evergrande executives to prison terms of up to 18 years on charges including illegally taking public deposits and fraud, the court said.

Evergrande group was fined 8.82 billion yuan ($1.85 billion) and Evergrande Real Estate Group was fined 7 billion yuan ($1.45 billion), the court said in a statement.

Hui pleaded guilty in April to various charges including illegal absorption of public deposits, fraud and bribery after he was arrested in China.

China Evergrande, founded in 1996, defaulted on its debts in 2021.

China now suffers from an oversupply of modern properties. (Reuters: Aly Song)

It was the world's most heavily indebted real estate developer before it was ordered to liquidate its assets.

China's fix for property crisis rewards marathon runners Local governments in China are offering marathon runners, AI experts and tennis players subsidies to purchase unwanted properties amid a lingering real estate downturn.

Authorities in Hong Kong and mainland China earlier said their investigations found Evergrande had manipulated its financial data.

Tactics used included prematurely booking revenue from property sales before completion and delivery of the apartments to buyers.

Revenues were overstated by roughly $US80 billion ($112 billion) over 2019 and 2020, they said.

The Chinese property market in 2026 is undergoing a deep structural shift from speculative hyper-growth into a permanent "stable contraction".

The Chinese real estate industry is struggling with an oversupply of inventory, while adjusting to a new economic reality where real estate is no longer China's primary engine of wealth.

Wires/ABC

World.title: Turnbull-backed battery proposal sets off sparks in Doreen
World.content:
PoliticsVictoriaCity life Turnbull-backed battery proposal sets off sparks in Doreen Adam Carey August 20, 2026 — 7:50pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

A renewable energy company chaired by former prime minister Malcolm Turnbull plans to build a large-scale battery on bushfire-prone land in Melbourne’s green wedges, alarming nearby residents who lived through the devastating Black Saturday fires of 2009. The proposed lithium-ion battery energy storage system could potentially store enough electricity to power almost 90,000 homes for a day. It would be built at an estimated cost of $500 million. Locals Sarah Hunter, Alicia Hynes, Barbara Marshall, Gareth Davies and Mel Nelson stand opposite the proposed big battery site. Ruby Alexander But the project has startled the small semi-rural communities of Doreen and Arthurs Creek on Melbourne’s north-eastern fringe, where residents only learnt of the proposal when a handful of neighbours were contacted by a communications agency on Tuesday. The Middle Hut BESS project, which had been kept under wraps until this week, is at an advanced stage of planning, with its developers, Turnbull Renewables, poised to apply directly to the state government for a planning permit next month.



Turnbull Renewables said the property had been chosen because it sat beneath two high-voltage transmission lines, meaning the battery could be plugged directly into Melbourne’s energy grid. “The site sits along the existing 330kV and 220 kV high-voltage transmission lines, the backbone of Victoria’s electricity network … [It] has been strategically chosen to store and dispatch energy close to metropolitan Melbourne,” the company said. It said the site was one of few along the transmission line corridor with the environmental conditions needed to support a battery system, and had been positioned away from homes. The battery system would cover about 14 hectares of what is currently mostly paddocks. But the site is also in a green wedge area that is zoned for its environmental significance and is designated as bushfire prone. A creek running through the property has Aboriginal cultural heritage value. The terrain is hilly and accessible only by a narrow gravel road.



Sarah Hunter lives on Middle Hut Road, where she and her husband run a small egg farm more than a kilometre away from the proposed battery site. She was not informed of the project on Tuesday; she learned about it through a local chat group. Hunter said the battery system would industrialise the mostly agricultural area, characterised by its rolling hills and native wildlife, and used as a foraging area for the critically endangered swift parrot. “There is a place for batteries but not in the middle of a hilly area in the green wedge with a bushfire overlay,” she said. Related Article Opinion

Travel tips What happens when your EV runs low on a regional road trip? I found out Ben Groundwater Travel writer “It’s like a transformation of this beautiful area in the foothills of the Kinglake mountains. When you put in a big industrial site, that’s really damaging.”



Arthurs Creek resident Gareth Davies lives a few kilometres away, on a property at the foot of Mount Sugarloaf that came under direct attack on Black Saturday. “I just don’t think it’s the right place,” he said. “Everybody would say that, like it’s a NIMBY thing, but my concern is it’s a known bushfire-prone area. I could barely get insurance. I had to ring around like you wouldn’t believe to get insurance here because of the risk that the actuaries put on this area.” Middle Hut BESS is the first Victorian project for Turnbull Renewables, a company chaired by Malcolm Turnbull and founded by his wife, Lucy Turnbull. It has previously delivered two hydropower projects in NSW. Malcolm Turnbull told The Age the battery system would store excess wind and solar power generated during the day and dispatch it at night. “Storage is absolutely critical for the energy transition,” he said. “With more and more of our energy coming from wind and solar, and particularly solar storage, the ability to essentially time-shift electrons from the middle of a sunny day to the evening, is really vital.”



Former prime minister Malcolm Turnbull says the Middle Hut BESS will assist the energy transition. Dominic Lorrimer The former Coalition prime minister, who left politics in 2018, said the developers had reached out to the local community, and would host a public information session later this month. “We are confident that this is a good project. It’ll be good for all of us,” he said. Related Article Energy Renewables are slashing power prices, but energy chiefs fear it may not last The project is expected to be considered by Planning Minister Sonya Kilkenny under the significant economic development provisions of the planning scheme.



A Victorian government spokesperson said the Department of Transport and Planning had not received an application for the project, and that all proposals were considered on their merits. “Green wedges play an important role in supporting agriculture, jobs, tourism and open space around Melbourne, which is why we are strengthening protections for them,” the spokesperson said. A Nillumbik Council spokesperson said they were aware of the proposal but it would not be assessed by council. “We believe the proposal will need to be publicly advertised, giving residents and other interested parties an opportunity to make a submission or object,” they said. According to Turnbull Renewables’ project timeline, construction would begin in 2028 and the battery would be operational by 2029.



A fire damaged Neoen Energy’s Victorian big battery project in July 2021. The fire burned for three days. Channel 7 Middle Hut BESS would be one of the largest lithium batteries in Melbourne, with a proposed capacity of 290MW/1160MWh. A small handful of industrial-scale batteries have already been built around Melbourne’s fringes, including the Melbourne Renewable Energy Hub in Plumpton, Rangebank BESS in Cranbourne West and the Victorian Big Battery near Geelong. Editor's pick Opinion

Victorian election Zero policies and a blank page: Pauline Hanson doesn’t look serious about Victoria Chip Le Grand State political editor The Victorian Big Battery caught fire and burned for three days in 2021. Turnbull Renewables acknowledged Middle Hut BESS was proposed for a bushfire-prone area and said a fire-risk assessment would form part of its application. It said it was engaging with the CFA. World.title: Police commissioner apologises for miscommunication after family told that deceased bushwalker was alive
World.content:
Updated NationalNSWTragedy Police commissioner apologises for miscommunication after family told that deceased bushwalker was alive Riley Walter and Jack Gramenz Updated August 20, 2026 — 7:49pm ,first published 11:47am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

NSW Police will investigate a series of failures that resulted in officers mistakenly informing the family of missing bushwalker Lily Hooper that the 18-year-old had been found alive after an eight-day search in the state’s Southern Highlands. Commissioner Mal Lanyon on Thursday was forced to apologise for the miscommunication that devastated her grieving parents, who, moments earlier, had celebrated what they believed was a miraculous survival. Loading For almost 20 minutes on Thursday, Hooper’s family believed she had been found alive in dense bushland, before being told police were still working to determine her condition. Shortly after, police confirmed she had been found dead. “I don’t know exactly what was said to her parents at the time, but obviously her condition, when she was located, the initial information that had been reported and was communicated, was that she was alive,” Lanyon said.



A police officer at the search base, on the edge of the Nattai National Park, told Hooper’s parents, Jim and Kirrily Hooper, that the teenager was alive after an SES volunteer found her during a ground search. An elated Jim Hooper told reporters that he had never given up hope that his daughter would be found alive. On the eighth day of searching, he had laid a “charm” – his daughter’s guitar and a pack of Tim Tams – under the marquee the family had turned into a makeshift home since August 12. It was to beckon their daughter out of the bush. Missing hiker Lily Hooper was found dead after an eight-day search in the NSW Southern Highlands. NSW Police “She’s coming home,” he said through tears before loved ones celebrated at the search base. “I’ve been beside myself ... we found her.”



The miscommunication may have been sparked by a radio code believed to be used by SES searchers to report that a body has been found, in which they refer to full, half or empty water bottles to signal whether a person is alive in the event family members may be monitoring the radio. A half bottle of water is believed to indicate a person’s condition is unclear. Hooper’s mother said police had told her she was found alive with half a bottle of water in her possession. Police do not use the code during their own searches. Australian Army personnel who participated in the rescue operation are addressed on Thursday. Kate Geraghty “That miscommunication, I unashamedly apologise for any additional trauma that may have caused Lily’s family, but certainly for the embarrassment and confusion that caused,” Lanyon said, adding that police sought to correct the information at the earliest opportunity. “The miscommunication, obviously, was born out of elation that Lily had been found and her condition at that time was such that searchers were relieved and certainly those at the command base were elated.”



NSW SES Assistant Commissioner Colin Malone said information transmitted over radio communications could be broken up in remote areas. Lanyon on Thursday afternoon apologised to NSW Premier Chris Minns, who had earlier announced to a parliamentary budget estimates committee that Hooper was alive after he received the incorrect information. SES volunteers involved in the search for Lily Hooper. Kate Geraghty “I’ve got some terrible news, and I apologise to the committee. But it seems as if the early advice was wrong, and Lily’s body’s been found, and she’s been found deceased,” Minns said. The information was passed from police to the premier via Police Minister Yasmin Catley, which Lanyon said was not unusual for a high-profile investigation.



“The communication may have passed through a number of hands,” he said. “We will obviously look at that communication, how it took place, with a view to making sure we confirm that.” Lily Hooper began her hike on the Bonnum Pic Walking Trail on August 12. Kate Geraghty Lanyon had spoken to NSW SES Commissioner Mike Wassing and would review the failure, he said. “This is not a circumstance I would like to see repeated,” Lanyon said.



“What’s important now is we look at the communication between all agencies to make sure we improve it.” Almost 1000 searchers had scoured dense bush in the national park looking for Hooper since she was reported missing on August 1, having left her home in Sydney’s south-west that morning to hike the Bonnum Pic walking trail. The beginning of the trail. Kate Geraghty Police officers on horseback, motorcycles and from several units searched alongside Australian Defence Force personnel, NSW State Emergency Services volunteers and Rural Fire Service firefighters. Helicopters and thermal imaging technology had also been used during the search for the teenager, who had remained in contact with her family on the day she went missing. Police found her Hyundai parked at the bottom of the challenging Bonnum Pic trail shortly after her family reported her missing.



Authorities on Thursday evening were working to retrieve Hooper’s body from dense bush that Lanyon said could not be accessed via police helicopter. Her cause of death is yet to be determined and will be subject to a coronial investigation. Specialist officers were exploring the possibility of carrying Hooper’s body out of the bush, given the difficulty to access the site where she was found, which was not on a clear walking track, and was a significant distance from her car. It is unclear what injuries, if any, she sustained or when she died. The rescue operation combed through the Nattai National Park, south-west of Sydney. NSW State Emergency Service “We’ll now work through a process, whether it’s manually, whether it’s on foot, to retrieve her body,” Lanyon said. “We’d like to bring her back to be with her family.”



NSW Opposition Leader Kellie Sloane, who had earlier, citing media reports, posted on social media that the teenager had been found alive, said Hooper’s death was heartbreaking and an unimaginable loss. “So many people had been hoping for Lily’s safe return and today’s news will be difficult and deeply felt,” she said. Federal Opposition Leader Angus Taylor, Hooper’s local member, published and then deleted a social media post indicating she had been found alive, later saying the incorrect reports of her survival made the family’s loss even worse. “We can only imagine what Lily’s family is going through right now. Such news would be a nightmare for any parent, and we grieve for Lily’s wider family,” Taylor told parliament. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said the family’s loss was an unspeakable tragedy.



“Lily Hooper had so much more to offer the world. Her passing, I have no doubt, will be felt very deeply,” he told parliament. “Our thoughts are of course with her family and loved ones on what is an incredibly sad and difficult day.” MPs also rose for a moment’s silence.
